Discovering the Third Doctor, the Daleks chased him in the ''Jefferson'' to Sydney Harbour Bridge, where Lt Davis destroyed the Daleks by dropping a live cable on the submarine from above. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[Sub Zero (comic story)|*Sub Zero]]'')

The Daleks, having observed the destruction of their forces on Earth, used a time vector to transport the TARDIS to Skaro, where they planned to perform an operation on the Doctor which would mentally turn him into a Dalek. The Doctor and his companion [[Finney]] escaped into the jungle, where they used a herd of [[Dinosaur (The Planet of the Daleks)|dinosaur-like creatures]] to destroy the Daleks. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[The Planet of the Daleks (comic story)|The Planet of the Daleks]]'')

==== Further battles ====
The Daleks took over the [[Homeworld|home planet]] of the [[Anthaurk]], forcing them to move to the [[Minerva system]] and begin a military focused culture. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Fall of Yquatine (novel)}})

At some point, a Dalek ship was shot down in a war, crash landing on the planet [[Red Rocket Rising]]. The Eighth Doctor [[deduce]]d that [[Professor]] [[Martez]] had turned human beings into "[[Mutant Dalek]]s" in his experiments to make humans more like Daleks using deceased but intact Daleks and technology taken from the ship. Years afterwards, a group of Daleks with short supplies and badly damaged from fighting were under the leadership of a [[Dalek Supreme]], and responded to a signal sent by Professor Martez, pretending to take the survivors of the [[asteroid]]-stricken world Red Rocket Rising to another planet.

In reality, the Daleks deflected the asteroid to destroy Martez' experiments, whom had deviated from the idea of Dalek blood purity, and failed. They planned to detonate their [[Dalek command ship (Blood of the Daleks)|command ship]] to destroy the Mutant Dalek base to ensure that the blood of the Daleks remained pure, and after that they would exterminate all humans on the planet. An explosion inside the command ship cancelled the detonation, causing the ship to go off course, saving [[Eileen Klint]]'s people thanks to [[Tom Cardwell]]. Despite this, the Daleks decided to destroy the mutants personally. A full-scale Dalek battle followed, with both Dalek groups determined to completely wipe out the other. With the help of the humans, both groups of Daleks wiped each other out. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Blood of the Daleks (audio story)}})

In [[45th century]] [[Stockbridge]], a rain was mutating the villagers into [[zombie]] slaves of the Daleks. They tried to turn the Doctor into a Dalek and use his TARDIS to help conquer the universe, but failed and they were defeated. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Plague of the Daleks (audio story)}})

=== Dalek-Movellan War ===
{{Main|Dalek-Movellan War}}
{{Section stub|[[Series 3 (TNCM)]]}}
[[File:SuicideMission.jpg|thumb|[[Bomber Dalek]]s on the march.([[TV]]: {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}})|left]]
According to the [[Celestial Intervention Agency]]'s research, during a time when the Dalek Empire was divided under the control of two Emperors, the Daleks were attacked by the [[Movellan]]s. One [[Emperor Dalek (The Dalek Problem)|Emperor]] was killed by the Movellans leaving the [[Dalek Prime|other]], who had been based on Skaro, in charge of the entire empire. This hampered the Daleks' tactics, as the Emperor was unable to keep track of forces that had been under the other's control. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Dalek Problem (novel)}})

During [[Borusa (The Five Doctors)|Borusa]]'s quest for immortality, a [[Dalek (The Five Doctors)|Grey Dalek]] was [[Time Scoop]]ed into the [[Game of Rassilon (The Five Doctors)|Game of Rassilon]] and set against the [[First Doctor]] and [[Susan Foreman|Susan]]. The two managed to trick the Dalek into the ricochet of its own [[gunstick]], killing it. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Five Doctors (TV story)}}) The Time Lords later deduced that the abducted unit had come from the [[46th century]], during the [[Dalek-Movellan War]], and that its abduction had been one of the acts of aggression that had [[Origins of the Last Great Time War|triggered]] the [[Last Great Time War]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek Combat Training Manual (reference book)}})

Just as how the Daleks used both [[Bronze Dalek|bronze]] and [[Grey Dalek|grey casings]] in their war with the Movellans, ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Pilot (TV story)}}, {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}}) a [[Bronze Dalek (The Daleks Chase Walter the Worm)|Bronze Dalek]] and two [[Grey Dalek 1 (The Daleks Chase Walter the Worm)|Grey]] [[Grey Dalek 2 (The Daleks Chase Walter the Worm)|Daleks]] chased [[Walter the Worm]] in an attempt to exterminate him, only to fail. ([[WC]]: ''[[The Daleks Chase Walter the Worm (webcast)|The Daleks Chase Walter the Worm]]'') The [[Twelfth Doctor]] once arrived in [[War zone (The Pilot)|a war zone]] during the Dalek-Movellan conflict with [[Nardole]] and [[Bill Potts]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Pilot (TV story)}}) During the conflict, the Daleks made themselves into robots to try to better understand the Movellans. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek Combat Training Manual (reference book)}})

A [[Kembel faction|faction of Daleks]] returned to [[Kembel]] seeking to regain lost knowledge of time travel. They used a [[time bubble]] to send a Dalek back in time to attempt to assassinate the [[Mark Seven|First Movellan]], ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Triumph of Davros (audio story)}}) however it only succeeded in destroying the Space Security Service's time machine. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Wrong Woman (audio story)|The Wrong Woman]]'') The Kembel faction did succeed in recreating a [[Dalek time machine]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Triumph of Davros (audio story)}}) The war indeed was fought throughout time; ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Dalek Gambit (audio story)|The Dalek Gambit]]'') the Daleks mainly used [[time corridor]]s to travel through time, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}}) whereas Movellan ships used [[time warp]]s. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}})

The conflict soon resulted in a centuries-long stalemate, with each side's purely logical [[battle computer]] keeping them in deadlock. To circumvent this stalemate, the Daleks returned to Skaro, which had been abandoned, to find [[Davros]] so his biological mind could reprogram their battle computers to win the war, being followed by a rival Movellan expedition. The [[Fourth Doctor]] saw to the defeat of both factions, destroying the majority of the Dalek force after they made into [[Bomber Dalek]]s sent against the Movellan vessel. Davros was taken by the Daleks' liberated slaves to stand trial. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}})

The Daleks attempted to recapture Davros whilst he was being transported by an [[Earth Protection Corps]] vessel, also carrying the [[Tenth Doctor]], however interference by Movellan forces resulted in the Earth ship crashing on Kembel. There the Movellans captured the Doctor and Davros whilst the Kembel Daleks caught his companion [[Anya Kingdom]] and Earth Protection Major [[Keelan]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Dalek Defence (audio story)|The Dalek Defence]]'') The pair were attached to bombs and sent to infiltrate the Movellan vessel but were quickly exposed and thrown out along with the Doctor, so the Daleks recaptured them. After Davros announced an alliance between Daleks and Movellans against Earth via the [[pathweb]], the Kembel Supreme decided to work with the Doctor against Davros. However, Davros eventually revealed the alliance was just a front to attempt to infect the First Movellan with a virus.

The Doctor prevented the virus spreading into the Movellans beyond Kembel whilst Earth Protection forces summoned by Keelan overwhelmed the Daleks on Kembel and recaptured Davros. The Doctor subsequently stole the Kembel Daleks' time machine, and Anya destroyed the Supreme when it tried to stop him. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Triumph of Davros (audio story)}}) The war continued for another 90 years, until the Movellans developed a [[Movellan virus]] to defeat the Daleks, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}}) who had returned to their organic states. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}})

=== Imperial-Renegade Dalek war ===
==== The virus spreads, the schism begins ====
[[File:Open wide.jpg|thumb|A [[Dalek drone]] is brainwashed by one of [[Davros]]'s agents. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
In [[4590]], ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (novelisation)}}) with more and more Daleks dying from the [[Movellan virus]], ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Secret Lives of Monsters (short story)}}) a detachment of Daleks and [[Dalek Trooper|Troopers]] led by the [[Black Dalek Leader|Supreme Dalek]] embarked on a [[Duplicate Incident|rescue mission]] in hopes of their creator to find a cure for the virus. They also used a [[time corridor]] and a [[Dalek duplicate]] called [[Stien]] to trap the [[Fifth Doctor]] to duplicate him and his [[Companion]]s to assassinate the [[Time Lord]] High Council. However, the Doctor broke free of the duplication apparatus and turned Stien to his cause. Meanwhile, Davros turned several [[Dalek Trooper]]s and two [[Imperial Dalek|Daleks]] to his cause through mind control, only for the Supreme's Daleks to destroy the rebels. Both Davros and the Doctor unleashed the virus and the [[Dalek Battlecruiser|Dalek ship]] was destroyed by Stien. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}})

Nevertheless, Davros's work on analysing the virus had already been sent to [[Dalek Supreme Command]], allowing the Daleks to quickly develop a cure. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Secret Lives of Monsters (short story)}}) Both Davros and the Supreme Dalek also survived the event. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}}, [[PROSE]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (novelisation)}}) However, to avoid the virus, the Daleks had dispersed across the cosmos, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}}) which led to increased factionalism amongst the Dalek Empire. After Davros's actions officially opened up a schism, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (novelisation)}}) the divide amongst the Daleks left their never-ending war effort in ruins, with invasions and wars failing. The Daleks grew concerned at the growing divide amongst their kind, with the Daleks on Skaro, despite continuing to claim that they did not need "humanoid lifeforms", coming to believe that they needed to rescue Davros so their creator could provide them direction. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Innocence (audio story)}})

==== Necros and the trial ====
[[File: Daleks Necros.jpg|thumb|Daleks from [[Necros]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}})|alt=|left]]
Davros escaped to [[Necros]] and began to turn intelligent [[Suspended animation|cryogenically frozen]] people into [[Imperial Dalek]]s to conquer the universe. However, [[Takis (Revelation of the Daleks)|Takis]] called the Daleks to take Davros to stand trial. The [[Grey Dalek]]s fought their way past the Imperials to take Davros. He tried to get them to take the [[Sixth Doctor]], but they didn't recognise him. The Daleks' attempt to recondition the Imperials failed because of the Imperials' destruction by the Doctor and [[Orcini]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}}) However, the Time Lords did later ponder if some Necros Daleks survived and helped their creator cement his control on Skaro during his trial. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek Combat Training Manual (reference book)}})

According to one account, en route to Skaro the ship carrying Davros crashed on the planet [[Lethe (The Juggernauts)|Lethe]]. Davros was rescued, and he set himself up as 'Professor Vaso' and attempted to create a new machine, a [[Juggernaut]] based on a [[Mechanoid]] design. Lethe's atmosphere prevented the Supreme Dalek retrieving Davros directly, but its forces intercepted the Sixth Doctor's [[the Doctor's TARDIS|TARDIS]], forcing him to serve as an agent of the Daleks and stop Davros' researches and manipulations. The Doctor discovered two of Davros' Necros Daleks had survived the crash, but were destroyed following Davros' final gambit on the colony and the Supreme Dalek's intervention. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Juggernauts (audio story)|The Juggernauts]]'')

One account claimed that Davros was brought to Skaro for a trial but learned of a Thal spy named [[Lareen]] who had snuck aboard their ship. She tried to convince Davros to destroy his creations with a more powerful strain of the Movellan virus the Thals had developed, but, upon reaching Skaro, Davros denounced her and revealed the existence of the virus. Surprised that Davros had not unleashed the virus and believing he was worthy of becoming the Emperor, the Daleks of Skaro proclaimed Davros to be their leader and exterminated Lareen. Before Davros arrived and was gifted the rank, the Dalek Supreme was planning to take on the role of Emperor, ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Davros Mission (audio story)|The Davros Mission]]'') yet other accounts suggested there already of an Emperor on Skaro during this time.

[[File:Ice Pyramid (Emperor of the Daleks!).jpg|thumb|[[Grey Dalek]]s chasing after Davros on Spiridon ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Emperor of the Daleks! (comic story)}})]]
That account claimed that Davros was put on trial for his life before the Emperor on Skaro. As part of a scheme with his future self, the Sixth Doctor rescued Davros just before the Daleks carried out their sentence of death. The Doctor took Davros to [[Spiridon]], where he could lick his wounds and bide his time. The Doctor intended to lay the groundwork for a Dalek civil war and spoke to Davros of his future destiny as [[Emperor Dalek]]. When Daleks led by the Supreme Dalek landed on Spiridon with the [[Seventh Doctor]], Davros set his new army of Imperial Daleks against them, along with a [[Special Weapons Dalek]]. The Supreme Dalek was killed. The Imperials then took over Skaro, seemingly exterminating the Emperor, and Davros was instated as Emperor of the Daleks. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Emperor of the Daleks! (comic story)}})

A third account claimed there was no "legal" trial. Instead, the Daleks of Skaro brought Davros to them to see if he was able to solve the schism ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Innocence (audio story)}}) that had developed after the Movellan war. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (novelisation)}}) Disgusted that the Daleks were seemingly scared and had failed their potential, Davros nonetheless agreed to offer them direction. Firstly, he reflected on his childhood and the [[creation of the Daleks]] to teach the Daleks of their earliest days. The Daleks who had brought Davros to Skaro to provide them direction claimed to be working under the command of the Dalek Supreme, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Innocence (audio story)}}) yet the [[Black Dalek Leader]], by most accounts, was opposed to the idea of Davros having any command over the Empire. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}}, et. al)

==== Open warfare ====
{{Main|Imperial-Renegade Dalek Civil War}}
[[File:Dalek veterans.jpg|thumb|[[Renegade Dalek]]s who served [[Black Dalek Leader|the Supreme]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}})|left]]
No matter what account of Davros' trial was true, the Dalek Empire was eventually divided into two camps. With Davros as its Emperor, one faction developed into an [[Imperium]] of Daleks given [[White Dalek|white casings]] and mechanical upgrades, yet these "[[Imperial Dalek]]s" were seen as impure by the Black Dalek Leader, which led a faction of [[Grey Dalek]]s that came to be known as the "[[Renegade Dalek|the Renegade faction]]" ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}}, et. al) on Davros's order; he decried the separatists under the Supreme as "renegades" for refusing to bow before him. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}})These two sides clashed in what became known as the "[[Imperial-Renegade Dalek Civil War]]". The Imperium secured control over Skaro, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}}, et. al) though the Renegades later claimed the world controlled by Davros was not the original Skaro. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|War of the Daleks (novel)}}

At some point, the Grey Daleks encountered the Sixth Doctor and [[Peri Brown]] on the planet [[Omnia]], which they had conquered after the [[Battle of Destiny]]. The Doctor made it his mission to free the planet from Dalek control, which was being supported by their puppet leader, [[Carmen Rega]]. The occupation was commanded by a [[Dalek Supreme (Emissary of the Daleks)|Dalek Supreme]] and aided by a [[Special Weapons Dalek (Emissary of the Daleks)|Special Weapons Dalek]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Emissary of the Daleks (audio story)}}) Davros and his [[Imperial Dalek]]s travelled back to the [[Battle of Waterloo]] in an attempt to change history but were thwarted by the Sixth Doctor. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Curse of Davros (audio story)}})

Serving under the command of the [[Dalek Prime]], which held the title of Emperor for the Renegade Daleks, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|War of the Daleks (novel)}} the Black Dalek Leader continued to lead the Renegade faction as the Supreme Dalek. However, the factionalism that had started after the Movellan war continued to divide the Dalek race, as the Renegade faction was not a united force, with some pockets of the faction not even declaring hostilities against Davros. During the war against Davros' faction, the Supreme hoped to find a way to unite its faction, eventually deciding it would need to kill the Doctor to bring about such a future. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (novelisation)}})

[[File:Dalek Shuttle in school yard.jpg|thumb|An Imperial [[Dalek shuttle]] landing in [[1963]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
During the war, the Imperial and Renegade Daleks both headed to [[Earth]] in [[1963]] to claim the [[Hand of Omega]]. The Imperials controlled [[H. Parson]], while the Renegades used [[Judith Winters]] as their [[battle computer]] and "allied" with [[the Association]]. The two factions waged a lengthy [[Shoreditch Incident|battle]] at [[Shoreditch]]. Aided by the [[Special Weapons Dalek]], the Imperial Daleks won, almost wiping out the Renegades aside from the Supreme. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}}) During the battle, one Imperial Dalek was transported to [[2016]] by a [[Time rift|rift]] in time at [[Coal Hill School]]. It learnt of the outcome of the battle and attempted to travel back to forewarn its comrades. It was stopped by the efforts of [[Ace]] and [[Andrea Quill|Quill]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[In Remembrance (audio story)|In Remembrance]]'')

The Imperial Daleks took the Hand of Omega, as the [[Seventh Doctor]] had planned all along. Davros plotted to ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}}) detonate the second sun of the Daleks' homeworld Skaro with the Hand, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Stranger (short story)}}) giving the Daleks the power of unlimited time travel. In the Imperial Daleks' time zone, he did so, causing it to go supernova. This action, however, destroyed the planet and the Imperial fleet, as the Doctor had programmed the Hand to do. On Earth, the Doctor talked the last Renegade Dalek, the black Supreme Dalek, into self-destructing. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}}) He did think to himself that, in reality, the Supreme was not the last of its kind and merely said that to convince the Dalek into destroying itself. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (novelisation)}})

=== A new empire ===
==== From the ashes of the civil war ====
Following the destruction of Skaro, Dalek battlecruisers continued to protect the area of the galaxy where Skaro used to be, even though it was now desolate. The Doctor briefly visited this part of space after encountering peace-loving Daleks in an alternate universe. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[The Ripple Effect (short story)|The Ripple Effect]]'')

[[File:Primepic 4.jpg|thumb|left|The [[Dalek Prime]], ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Shadow of Humanity (comic story)}}) who was credited to be the leader of the Renegade Daleks and winner of the civil war in one account of history. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|War of the Daleks (novel)}}]]
According to some accounts, the [[Dalek Prime]]'s [[Renegade Dalek]]s emerged victorious, now referring to themselves as the true Imperials. Davros' escape pod was acquired by a garbage ship, the [[Quetzel]], which the [[Eighth Doctor]] and [[Sam Jones]] also ended up on. A group of [[Thal]]s arrived, with the intention of using Davros to effectively turn them into Daleks so they could fight the Daleks better. A Dalek force arrived and took the Quetzel to a planet called Skaro. The [[Dalek Prime]] claimed that this was the original Skaro, and that the planet the Doctor had destroyed was a decoy called [[Antalin]]. The Dalek Prime knew that some of its own Daleks were loyal to Davros and put Davros on trial to flush them out. A battle ensued and the Dalek Prime emerged victorious. A Dalek factory ship was lost to the Time Vortex, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|War of the Daleks (novel)}} with the Doctor believing it was the ship that would crash on [[Vulcan]] and be dealt with by his [[Second Doctor|second incarnation]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|War of the Daleks (novel)}}; [[TV]]: {{cs|The Power of the Daleks (TV story)}}) Davros was apparently executed, though a [[Spider Dalek]] loyal to him had promised to pose as his executioner and teleport him to safety, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|War of the Daleks (novel)}} which Davros's later survival would appear to confirm. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}} et al.)

According to one dissenting account, it was also around this point post-civil war point in Dalek history, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The History of the Daleks (short story)}}) rather than prior to the [[Dalek-Movellan War]] and revival of [[Davros]] as most accounts tended to hold, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}, [[COMIC]]: {{cs|Bringer of Darkness (comic story)}}, etc.) that the Dalek Emperor's [[Human Factor]] gambit occurred, backfiring into a "final end" for the Dalek race as it became engulfed in the original [[Dalek Civil War]] arranged by the [[Second Doctor]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The History of the Daleks (short story)}}) Although the Doctor thought it plausible that some Daleks would survive the cataclysm and rebuild, he was hopeful that they would never again reach the same heights as before. He further believed that the Dalek Prime was finally dead, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Evil of the Daleks (novelisation)}}) unaware that its backup systems had kicked on and the lights of the Emperor still shined through the night of Skaro. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Evil of the Daleks (TV story)}})

Another account of the end of the Imperial-Renegade Civil War held that Davros' escape pod entered the [[time vortex]] and was found by a Nekkistani ship. The Eighth Doctor, [[Samson Griffin]] and [[Gemma Griffin]] found the Nekkistani ship in the vortex and the Griffins boarded the ship to investigate. Davros exacted his revenge by sending them back to Earth, wiping the Doctor's memory of them and operating on the TARDIS. Samson was sent home and Gemma became part of the "resistance" to the new race of Daleks Davros made on Earth. They conquered the planet, leaving only the area where Samson lived free from Dalek control.

When the Doctor, [[Charley Pollard]] and [[C'rizz]] returned from the [[Divergent Universe]], Davros was waiting for them. Davros' mind had become fractured between his own personality and that of "the Emperor". A series of events led to the Doctor actually giving the Daleks their Emperor and letting them leave Earth. Davros left Earth with his Daleks, the Emperor personality dominant. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Terror Firma (audio story)}})

[[File:Black Dalek (DAU)-0.jpg|thumb|right|A [[Black Dalek (Daleks Among Us)|Black Dalek]] officer on [[Azimuth]] ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Daleks Among Us (audio story)}})]]
A third account stated that Davros' escape pod crash-landed on [[Azimuth]], which the Seventh Doctor and [[Ace]] had, at least seemingly, liberated from Dalek occupation twenty local years prior. In truth, a Dalek force under a [[Black Dalek (Daleks Among Us)|Black Dalek]] reminded hidden on the world. After Davros landed and attempted to make contact with other Daleks in the universe, he encountered the Seventh Doctor again. He contacted Daleks that took over planet and created a clone of his younger self [[Falkus (Daleks Among Us)|Falkus]] as Davros' son. When learned about the [[Persuasion machine]] from [[Will Arrowsmith]], Davros wanted it to reassert his control over the Daleks. However, the machine was destroyed by [[Elizabeth Klein]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Daleks Among Us (audio story)}})

A fourth account, which may have been a result of the changes to history caused during the [[Kotturuh crisis]], suggested that after Davros fled the war, one [[Emperor of the Restoration|Dalek Supreme]] exterminated all other members of the [[Dalek Council]] ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Restoration Empire (short story)}}) and was elected the new [[Dalek Emperor]] of the Imperial Daleks. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}) He founded the [[Restoration Empire]] and modelled himself on a former emperor, building a gold casing which augmented his brain capacity. Under his command, the Daleks remade Skaro. To further harken back to the old empire, he brought back the Silver Daleks as Drones. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Restoration Empire (short story)}}) This Emperor was advised by the [[Dalek Prime Strategist]], which claimed to be the oldest Dalek alive. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Defender of the Daleks (comic story)}})

==== The Dalek Hive ====
{{main|Dalek Hive}}
[[File:Dalek Supreme of the Dalek Hive.jpg|thumb|left|The Daleks of the [[Dalek Hive]]. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Fire and Brimstone (comic story)}})|left]]
According to another account, after the [[Shoreditch Incident|destruction of Skaro]], the last surviving Daleks reorganised themselves into a mobile [[Dalek Hive]] led by a [[Supreme Dalek (Fire and Brimstone)|gigantic Dalek Supreme]].

While sailing past the [[Magellan Cluster]], the Dalek Hive was attacked by a ship which had fallen through a [[time rift|rift]] from [[Barusa's universe|another universe]]. After wiping out all of its aggressive inhabitants save one, the Daleks were horrified to discover the insectoid mutants were [[Dalek (Barusa's universe)|the Daleks]] of this other universe. Becoming paranoid about being invaded ''en masse'' by "unalike" Daleks from parallel realities, they threw their all into the idea of a preemptive strike against the rest of the [[Omniverse]].

To do so, they had their android [[Marquez]] interfere with [[human]]ity in the [[51st century]], who were creating an [[Crivello's Cauldron|engineered sun called Crivello's Cauldron]] similar to the [[Eye of Harmony]]. He ensured that the [[Eighth Doctor]] got involved, thereby making sure that the biodata of an individual [[time sensitivity|time sensitive]] would become bonded to the Cauldron. When the Doctor and [[Izzy Sinclair|Izzy]] visited the Cauldron at a later date, the Daleks took control of [[Icarus Falling]] — one of the artificial worlds now orbiting the Cauldron — and used the Doctor as a conduct to take control of the Cauldron and make it collapse into a [[black hole]] which could then be turned into an interdimensional gateway.

They had failed to realise that various forces from other universes were waiting for just such an opportunity to swarm in — including the spider-like Daleks as well as the [[Great Vampire]]s. The Dalek Hive and its fleet were attacked as they began to cross through the wormhole, quickly proving no match for their enemies, with the Dalek Supreme being destroyed by the alternative Daleks. Ultimately, the Doctor got [[Ptolemy Muttonchops]], an avatar of the Cauldron, to take conscious control of the Cauldron's power and cause it to go [[supernova]], destroying the Daleks entirely. He discovered that [[Matrix Rassilon|Rassilon]] had orchestrated this entire sequence of events, paying the [[Threshold]] an unknown prize for them to embed [[Sister Chastity|an operative]] on Icarus Falling and ensure that those events would come to pass, wiping out the Daleks once and for all. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Fire and Brimstone (comic story)}})

==== Renewal of the Dalek Empire ====
{{Section stub|Their cameo in ''[[Seasons of Fear (audio story)|Seasons of Fear]]'', which is explained in {{cs|The Time of the Daleks (audio story)}}, needs to be added}}
[[File:Kar-Charrat.jpg|left|thumb|[[Dalek Supreme (The Genocide Machine)|The Supreme]] on [[Kar-Charrat]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Genocide Machine (audio story)}})]]
On the first stage of their new empire, the Daleks invaded [[Kar-Charrat]] to gain knowledge data from the [[Library on Kar-Charrat]] with their [[Dalek test subject|Test subjects]]. They created the first test subject, but it went insane. However, the second test subject was able to gain knowledge from the [[Wetworks facility]] and gained a respect for non-Dalek life and refused to obey orders to kill and destroy. It was destroyed by the [[Special Weapons Dalek]]. The Daleks were stopped by the [[Seventh Doctor]] and his companion [[Ace]] who planted explosives which killed the Daleks and destroyed the Wetworks facility, freeing the [[Kar-Charratan]]s. However the [[Dalek Supreme]] retreated to its [[Dalek Destroyer|mothership]] and reported failure to the [[Emperor Dalek]], who was infuriated and ordered it to self-destruct. It did and the Emperor decided another plan would be completed. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Genocide Machine (audio story)}}) Unknown to the Doctor, the Daleks gained information which they would use in their invasions including about the human mind and [[Project Infinity]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Invasion of the Daleks (audio story)}}, ''[[Project Infinity]]'')

The second stage of the Dalek Empire was to take control of [[Gallifrey]]. The Daleks led by the [[Black Dalek]] removed the [[Etra Prime]] from time and space so that they could mine the [[Apocalypse Element]] from the planet kidnapping a Monan and Time Lord delegation including [[Lady President]] [[Romana II|Romanadvoratrelundar]]. Twenty years later the Daleks sent Etra Prime on a collision course with the planet [[Archetryx]], which was hosting a temporal treaty attended by twenty of the [[Temporal Powers]]. The Dalek force invaded Gallifrey and added their own mental energy to the [[Eye of Harmony|Eye]], which did contain the Element. The Daleks were defeated by the [[Sixth Doctor]]. Despite that defeat, The Daleks detonated the Element in the [[Seriphia Galaxy]], destroying everything within it, and allowed the Daleks to establish a power base and to control over a million Skaros for their new empire. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Apocalypse Element (audio story)}})

During the early days of the [[2150s Dalek invasion of Earth|Dalek invasion and occupation]] of [[Earth]] in [[22nd century]] a lone Dalek in [[2158]] [[Kansas]] had been damaged by weapon fire which penetrated its casing, allowing for a parasitic [[wasp]] to enter the body. Once the Dalek returned to base, it was deemed damaged and sent to the repair bay where its genetic material was to be analysed. This was part of the Daleks' standard practice of taking the [[DNA]] to the reproductive factories for the breeding of more Daleks. It was at this point that the [[Dalek Prime|Dalek Emperor]] from an alternate future arrived and informed them of a great catastrophe that would befall them and provided them a cure; an insecticide that would prevent a so-called "Mutant Phase" from occurring.

The [[Fifth Doctor]] and [[Nyssa]] arrived to help a [[Thal]] professor [[Ptolem]] and his friend [[Ganatus (The Mutant Phase)|Ganatus]] for the research over the [[Mutant Phase]]. This had caused the Daleks transformation into nearly indestructible creatures. The Dalek Emperor forced the Doctor to return to the [[22nd century]] to stop the mutant phase's origins and destroyed [[Skaro]] by exploding the planet in the [[43rd century]] when it came under attack by the [[Mutant Phase]]. The Emperor implanted his mind into Ganatus' to make sure Ptolem and the Doctor did their work. It was the Emperor who was the cause of implementing an ineffective pesticide paradox. The Doctor convinced him not to change the past. The Emperor listened and negated the [[alternate timeline]] and the Mutant Phase and the Emperor was erased from existence. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Mutant Phase (audio story)}})

The final stage of the Empire began when the Daleks launched over a thousand Dalek Saucers into the [[Time Vortex]]. A [[Temporal Extinction Device]] was deployed in a time fissure by a Dalek vessel within the Time Vortex. This caused instability. The Dalek time ship was swamped by a tidal wave of temporal energy. They were trapped in a [[Time loop]] however one pilot and [[Dalek Strategist (The Time of the Daleks)|two strategists]] arrived to General [[Mariah Learman]] after using an escape [[Time corridor]]. The Daleks injected her with drugs and transformed her into a Dalek. They invaded Earth in the [[17th century]]. These forces were stopped by the Doctor, who left them trapped in the vortex. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Time of the Daleks (audio story)}}) The [[Time Lord]]s later made a deal with the Daleks that allowed them to leave the Time Vortex. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Neverland (audio story)|Neverland]]'')

When the Daleks tracked [[Mila|Patient Zero]] to the [[Amethyst Viral Containment Station]] in the past, the [[Dalek Time Controller]] commanded a mission sent there, planning to move the station through time to the Daleks. The [[Sixth Doctor]] damaged their operations and left them trying to fend off an explosion. However, the Time Controller realised the explosion at the Amethyst Viral Containment Station had caused the viruses to be scattered through time and allowed it to happen. The Doctor believed the Time Controller had been destroyed in the explosion, ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Patient Zero (audio story)|Patient Zero]]'') It was actually blasted back in time. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Lucie Miller (audio story)}}/{{cs|To the Death (audio story)}})

==== Second Great Dalek Occupation ====
{{Main|Second Great Dalek Occupation}}

Having learnt of [[Project Infinity]] from the [[Library on Kar-Charrat]], the Emperor planned to hijack it and bring forth an army of alternate Daleks who had conquered their own universe. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Project Infinity (audio story)}}) To this end, he ordered the conquest of [[Mutter's Spiral]], beginning with [[Dalek invasion of Vega VI|the invasion]] of [[Vega VI]], from which he mined [[veganite]] ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Invasion of the Daleks (audio story)}}) to boost the power of Project Infinity when the time came. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Project Infinity (audio story)}}) The Daleks' invasion was opposed by the [[Earth Alliance]], resulting in a massive war. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Invasion of the Daleks (audio story)}}, {{cs|The Human Factor (audio story)}}, {{cs|The Fearless: Part 1 (audio story)}}, {{cs|The Fearless: Part 2 (audio story)|Part 2}}, {{cs|The Fearless: Part 3 (audio story)|Part 3}}, {{cs|The Fearless: Part 4 (audio story)|Part 4}}) This period was known as the [[Second Great Dalek Occupation]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Return of the Daleks (audio story)}})

[[File:Project Infinity Daleks.jpg|thumb|right|The Daleks attack. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Project Infinity (audio story)}})]]
The Emperor and the [[Dalek Supreme (Invasion of the Daleks)|Dalek Supreme]] used [[Susan Mendes]] to give the new human slaves [[hope]] and increase their productivity, with her becoming known as "the Angel of Mercy" among the slaves, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Invasion of the Daleks (audio story)}}) although they were suspicious of he, and her friend [[Kalendorf]], and suspected some deception. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Project Infinity (audio story)}}) The Daleks duplicated Susan to divert Alliance assassins. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Fearless: Part 3 (audio story)}}) On Zaleria, the [[Dalek Scientific Division]] attempted to reverse-engineer the [[Spiridon (species)|Zalerians]]' [[invisibility]] and awaken the Dalek army on [[Spiridon|their planet]]. On his and Suz's visit to Zaleria, Kalendorf discovered the army and attempted to destroy it with the [[Seventh Doctor]]. However, the Daleks surrounded them and the Doctor surrendered to save Kalendorf, promising to help the Scientific Division's research. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Return of the Daleks (audio story)}}) Despite the failure of their first invasion attempt, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Fearless: Part 4 (audio story)}}) Earth eventually fell to the Daleks once more. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|"Death to the Daleks!" (audio story)}})

After ten years, Susan instigated a huge [[rebellion]] by the slaves across the Empire. This had been organised by Susan and Kalendorf via his telepathy, and had been anticipated by the Emperor ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|"Death to the Daleks!" (audio story)}}) who used to the cover of the rebellion to travel with the Dalek Supreme to [[Lopra Minor]] with their supply of veganite to make contact with [[The Mentor's universe|another universe]]. Susan was stunned and placed in suspended animation aboard the Emperor's vessel. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Project Infinity (audio story)}}) After hearing word of the rebellion, the Doctor realised history was playing out as it should and released a virus on Zaleria, which infected all the Daleks there with light wave sickness and restored the natives' invisibility. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Return of the Daleks (audio story)}}) The Earth Alliance, revived by the rebellion, attempted to defend Project Infinity but ultimately failed. The Emperor made contact with the [[the Mentor]]'s [[Alliance Dalek|Daleks]]. However the alternate Daleks judged the Daleks as evil and attacked ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Project Infinity (audio story)}}) and the Emperor entered a state of [[inertia]] to keep himself from being interrogated, leaving the Dalek Supreme to lead the Dalek Empire. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Dalek War: Chapter One (audio story)}})

==== War with the Mentor ====
{{Main|Enemy-Alliance Dalek War}}

The Mentor allied her Daleks with the Earth Alliance and together their forces pushed back the Daleks. After 6 years, the Daleks had fallen back to Earth's solar system. Kalendorf, now commander of the Earth Alliance, became uncomfortable with the Mentor's Daleks, believing they'd merely swapped one dictatorship for another, albeit a more outwardly benevolent one. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Dalek War: Chapter One (audio story)}})

Kalendorf made a deal with the Daleks for a truce and to turn on the Mentor, in return for which he arranged the retrieval of Susan Mendes whose body the Emperor had transferred its mind to. As Alliance forces were about to engage the Daleks in the solar system, he had Susan declare that the Angel of Mercy had returned and order the Earth Alliance to turn on the Mentor's Daleks. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Dalek War: Chapter One (audio story)}}, {{cs|Dalek War: Chapter Two (audio story)|Chapter Two}}, {{cs|Dalek War: Chapter Three (audio story)|Chapter Three}}) Kalendorf then surrendered Susan to the Daleks, so they could retrieve the Emperor's mind.

Years of war ensued, with the Daleks and Earth Alliance slowly forcing the Mentor's forces back into their own universe. Eventually the Mentor herself summoned Kalendorf to her universe where she conceded defeat, deciding that the war was pointless, and withdrew her forces back to her universe. The war over; an uneasy truce remained between the Daleks and Earth Alliance.

Kalendorf travelled to Dalek-occupied Earth to confront the Emperor. He discovered that it had chosen to remain in Susan's body permanently and had fully possessed her. Kalendorf grabbed her, telepathically reawakening Susan's mind and triggering a command he'd implanted in her before surrendering her: "Victory or Death". This triggered a signal across the entire Dalek command net, ordering all Dalek technology to self-destruct. This devastated the Daleks, killing the Emperor and Supreme, and much of the Galaxy, becoming known as the [[Great Catastrophe (The Exterminators)|Great Catastrophe.]] Kalendorf survived, believing the Daleks were defeated for good. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Dalek War: Chapter Four (audio story)}}) Many years later, he and the [[Eighth Doctor]] encountered a surviving Dalek in a museum on Vega VI dedicated to the Second Great Dalek Occupation. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Museum Peace (short story)|Museum Peace]]'')

==== Revival of the Dalek Empire ====
In the [[Seriphia Galaxy]], a Dalek outpost survived the Catastrophe by containing the signal to a single Dalek drone. This resulted in the Dalek's mind absorbing the Emperor and Susan's minds. It was declared the new Dalek Supreme. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Demons (audio story)}})

Approximately two thousand years after the Catastrophe, the Daleks had rebuilt and were plotting their return to Mutter's Spiral. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Dalek War: Chapter Four (audio story)}}) The Daleks triggered a crisis in the [[Galactic Union]] by spreading the NFS Plague in the [[Border Worlds]]. The Border Worlds eventually seceded from the Union to a form their own Confederation, and the Daleks approached them offering help with the Plague. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Exterminators (audio story)}}) The Daleks arranged the geoforming of the [[Graxis System]] for treatment facilities, bringing them into conflict with the [[Graxis Warden]]s, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Healers (audio story)}}) In truth, the Daleks' NFS treatment, [[Variant 7]], mutated Humans into Daleks to replenish the Daleks' forces. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Warriors (audio story)}}) As the Daleks tightened their hold over the Confederation, the surviving Wardens worked with Galactic Union agents [[Siy Tarkov]] and Galanar to gather evidence to warn the Union about the Daleks. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Survivors (audio story)}}, {{cs|The Demons (audio story)}}, {{cs|The Warriors (audio story)}})

They eventually travelled to [[Velyshaa]] to gather Kalendorf's psychic recordings, which Siy had previously witnessed, to evidence the Daleks' past conquests. The Supreme personally led forces to stop them, having been alerted by [[Elaria|a traitor in the group]], though they managed to transmit their evidence to [[Georgi Selestru]], a sympathetic Union Security Commander who they hoped could convince the Union to act. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Future (audio story)}}) The Daleks eventually outright occupied the Border Worlds entirely, leading to a Cold War between the new Dalek Empire and the Galactic Union. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Mutually Assured Survival (short story)|Mutually Assured Survival]]'')

==== Conflict with the Time Lords ====
===== Role in the War in Heaven =====
During the [[War in Heaven]], the Daleks were invited to [[Qixotl's auction]] for [[The Relic (Alien Bodies)|the Relic]], but the [[Kroton (species)|Krotons]] overpowered their representatives to take their place. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Alien Bodies (novel)}}) The [[Eighth Doctor]] and [[Sam Jones]] stopped the [[Dalek invasion of Tuvalu|Daleks' invasion]] of [[Tuvalu]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Unnatural History (novel)}}) The Daleks took part in the war in the [[Enclave]], with it being predicted they would be the first "new arrivals" to enter that conflict. ([[PROSE]]:{{cs|The Blue Angel (novel)}})

Although [[Homunculette]]'s thoughts showed otherwise ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Alien Bodies (novel)}}) and various other identities were posited by other accounts, ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Cobweb and Ivory (short story)|Cobweb and Ivory]]'', etc.) one possible identity of [[the Enemy]] was in fact the Daleks. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Quantum Archangel (novel)}}, ''[[The Taking of Planet 5 (novel)|The Taking of Planet 5]]'') One history of the Daleks written after the [[Last Great Time War]] claimed that the Time Lords had first decided to take action against the Daleks because they believed the coming of the Daleks "represented the emergence of the enemy they had long [[prophecy|prophesied]]". ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}})

However, one [[briefing]] described "[[Dalek mutant|xenophobic mutants]] travelling in their own personal war machines" as one of the several groups that some ''considered'' the Enemy, but who were in reality just one of the groups trying to take advantage of the War in Heaven for their own ends. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Pre-narrative Briefings (short story)|Pre-narrative Briefings]]'') In the [[post-War universe]], [[Anji Kapoor]] saw a Dalek in the [[time vortex]], ([[PROSE]]: ''[[The Last Resort (novel)|The Last Resort]]'') and one account implied the [[Great Black Eye]] to be the [[eyestalk]] of a Dalek. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Sometime Never... (novel)}})

Asking to see his future while looking into a [[Tomorrow Window]], one of the sights the Eighth Doctor saw was a city in ruins with a [[Dalek flying saucer]] above. Below, Daleks scanned the ruins. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Tomorrow Windows (novel)}}) With the Time Lords no longer present to quell time travel development in the lesser species, the Daleks had begun greatly growing in prominence, ([[PROSE]]: ''[[The Gallifrey Chronicles (novel)|The Gallifrey Chronicles]]'') although the Time Lords were eventually restored to power. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Tomorrow Windows (novel)}})

===== Shift in the timelines =====
{{Main|Kotturuh crisis}}

====== Investigating the truth ======
When the [[Tenth Doctor]] began rewriting history by poisoning the [[Kotturuh]] in the [[Dark Times]], ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Knight, The Fool and The Dead (novel)}}) he caused temporal fluctuations which rewrote timelines across the universe. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Guide to the Dark Times (short story)}}) As a result of this, the Restoration Empire, presided over by the Emperor of the Restoration and the Prime Strategist and still utilising the Silver Dalek design for Drones, did not appear to have fought the [[Last Great Time War]] yet. The Tenth Doctor, upon encountering the Restoration Empire, would identify its continued existence, and its Emperor's, as a "[[paradox]]", taking special note of the fact that this version of Dalek history seemed not to contain the Time War, ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Defender of the Daleks (comic story)}}) though it later became clear that the Restoration Empire pre-dated the Time War. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Exit Strategy (short story)}})

After receiving a message from an [[Dalek (The Last Message)|ancient Dalek drone]], which he deduced was a survivor of a Time Squad that had yet to travel back in time, the Emperor of the Restoration became aware of fluctuations in time involving the Doctor. He decided that he needed more information and thought of the [[Archive of Islos]] as a place to acquire it. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Last Message (short story)}}) The Emperor personally led the invasion of Islos, alongside the Strategist, several [[Dalek Commander|Commanders]] and a [[Dalek Executioner]]. However the [[Chief Archivian]] made a deal for the Archive's rescue, promising their rescuers the Daleks. Upon entering the Archive, the Emperor, Strategist, Executioner and two Commanders found it empty save the Archivians, who revealed their deal as an Entity emerged through a portal. ([[WC]]: ''[[The Archive of Islos (webcast)|The Archive of Islos]]'')

The Daleks fled the Entity and returned to Skaro to call upon the forces there. Their attacks proved ineffective, forcing the Emperor to order Skaro's evacuation. The Daleks withdrew, having [[Evacuation of Skaro|lost their home planet]], and sought reinforcements from [[the Sentinel of the Fifth Galaxy]]. The Strategist activated the Sentinel and was escorted to a dormant army of 10,000 Daleks. However the Sentinel had fallen under the Entity's influence, which had pre-empted the Daleks by its time sensitivity, and compromised the army. The Strategist self-destructed the facility and the Executioner led Daleks against the compromised Daleks that escaped. The Strategist advised another withdrawal, as the Daleks couldn't sustain further losses. ([[WC]]: ''[[The Sentinel of the Fifth Galaxy (webcast)|The Sentinel of the Fifth Galaxy]]'')

[[File:Planet of the Mechaniods.jpg|thumb|right|The [[Emperor of the Restoration]] and [[Mechanoid Queen]]. ([[WC]]: {{cs|Planet of the Mechanoids (webcast)}})]]
The Entity continued to tear through the Daleks, so the Strategist plotted to play it against the [[Mechonoid Empire]]. Appearing as though his empire had been destroyed, when in reality his forces were safe, ([[WC]]: {{cs|Day of Reckoning (webcast)}}) the Emperor travelled to [[Mechanus]], claiming to want the aid of the [[Mechanoid]]s, accompanied by the Strategist. In truth, they were luring the Entity there deliberately. ([[WC]]: {{cs|Planet of the Mechanoids (webcast)}}) The Prime Strategist and [[Mechanoid 2150]] managed to send the Entity back to its own dimension, though many Mechonoids were killed during the [[Battle of Mechanus|battle]]. The [[Mechanoid Queen]] told the Emperor and Strategist to flee, informing them that the might of the Mechanoid Empire would be coming after them. ([[WC]]: ''[[The Deadly Ally (webcast)|The Deadly Ally]]'')

After the Emperor and Strategist returned to Skaro, the Mechanoids arrived, believing they were the last two survivors of the Dalek race. The Emperor revealed that his forces were in fact alive, and the Daleks he'd recalled to Skaro and awoken from underground bunkers began to overwhelm the Mechanoids. The Queen and unit 2150 attempted to turn the Strategist against the Emperor, but he used 2150 to improve a Dalek beam projector. Thus, instead of sending the Emperor to the Entity's dimension like 2150 thought he would, the Strategist sent the entire Mechanoid army there, bringing about a Dalek victory. However, the Entity then managed to possess a ruined Mechanoid, telling the Emperor and Strategist that another threat was coming. ([[WC]]: {{cs|Day of Reckoning (webcast)}})

====== Locating the Doctors ======
Accordingly, the Daleks were attacked by the [[Hond]] after a failed attempt to ally with them. With Skaro itself in danger of falling to the Hond, the Strategist suggested the recruitment of the Doctor, ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Defender of the Daleks (comic story)}}) also planning to use him to help transport the Daleks back to the Dark Times, where their own timeships could not go, having discovered them as the source of the alterations to history. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Restoration Empire (short story)}}, {{cs|Exit Strategy (short story)}}) The Daleks captured the Tenth Doctor and brought him to Skaro. Reluctantly convinced by the Emperor, the Doctor worked with the Strategist and identified a way to pacify the Hond. Once he was done, some Daleks, led by a [[Grey Dalek (Defender of the Daleks)|Grey Dalek]], turned on him, yet he escaped with the help of the [[Thirteenth Doctor]]. With the Emperor demanding the Strategist to explain the Doctor's early escape, the Strategist suggested the Daleks use a different incarnation of the Doctor for the next part of their plan, such as the [[Eighth Doctor]]. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Defender of the Daleks (comic story)}})

The Emperor created a [[Dalek Time Squad|Time Squad]], led by the [[Dalek Time Commander]] and including the Strategist, an [[Dalek Executioner (The Guide to the Dark Times)|Executioner]] and a [[Scientist Dalek (The Guide to the Dark Times)|Scientist]], whose main mission was to investigate the fluctuations in time and rectify them to the Daleks' benefit. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Guide to the Dark Times (short story)}}) The Daleks captured the Eighth Doctor's TARDIS from Atharna, bringing him to them, ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[He Kills Me, He Kills Me Not (audio story)|He Kills Me, He Kills Me Not]]'') in order to manipulate him into offering his help to transport them to the Dark Times. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Restoration Empire (short story)}}) Despite the Executioner's desire to kill the Doctor, the Strategist took him before the Commander and they asked for his help in their investigation. They went to Wrax, nominally to analyse the rewriting of the planet's timeline however the Daleks also hoped to obtain the Devolver, a superweapon the Wraxians used to eliminate other civilisations.

Whilst the Strategist and the Doctor examined the Wraxians' gallery, the Commander, Executioner and Scientist met the Wraxian President who agreed to demonstrate the weapon for them and to consider an alliance. After the demonstration, she trapped the three Daleks and they realised she had betrayed them and intended to use the Devolver on them. The [[Silver Dalek|Dalek Drones]] were ordered to invade Wrax to stop her. The Doctor and Strategist worked together and managed to reach the President. The Doctor convinced the Daleks to let him negotiate, and talked the President into dismantling the Devolver in return for the Daleks' withdrawal. The Commander agreed, however secretly sent the Executioner back to Wrax to wipe out the Wraxians with the Devolver. The Doctor deduced the alterations to history originated in the Dark Times and connected his TARDIS to the Dalek timeship so they could travel back there. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Enemy of My Enemy (audio story)|The Enemy of My Enemy]]'')

====== Into the Dark Times ======
The Time Squad travelled back into the Dark Times with the Eighth Doctor. Having found the location of the source of the alterations to time to be [[Mordeela]], the Daleks brought the saucer to confront the Tenth Doctor's mercenary fleet over Mordeela, alongside a [[Vampire]] [[coffin ship]] commanded by the [[Ninth Doctor]], to stop him destroying the planet. This instigated the [[Battle of Mordeela]], which resulted in the Tenth Doctor's escape and the complete obliteration of Mordeela. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Knight, The Fool and The Dead (novel)}}, {{cs|All Flesh is Grass (novel)}}) Believing they'd failed to correct history, the Strategist and Scientist had the Time Squad harvest specimens from many species that were either extinct by their native time or had never previously existed, hoping to learn information they could use to their benefit and create a more biologically efficient form of Dalek - the [[Dalek Symbiont|Symbiont]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Restoration Empire (short story)}}, {{cs|Mission to the Known (short story)}}, {{cs|All Flesh is Grass (novel)}})

One of these races was the natives of [[Velosia]]. The Daleks arrived under the pretence of saving them from the Kotturuh, and convinced them to bring their greatest minds to the Daleks, which they then harvested. Later still, accompanied by the Eighth Doctor, the Daleks discovered an abandoned ship with a source of [[Huon]] energy. The Daleks attempted to absorb the Huon energy, but found themselves in difficulty till the Doctor helped them. They thanked him for being their saviour again, to his discomfort. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Tales of the Dark Times (comic story)}}) Though they side-lined him from their plots, the Daleks allowed the Eighth Doctor to accompany them on explorations, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|All Flesh is Grass (novel)}}) including an abandoned spaceship they discovered adrift in space. Whilst he was fascinated by the art aboard, the Daleks found a source of Huon energy and attempted to absorb it. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Tales of the Dark Times (comic story)}})

The Strategist and Scientist decided to focus on the creation of a [[Dalek Symbiont|Symbiont]] that would combine genetic material from the [[Great Vampire]]s with the Daleks, thus creating a Dalek mutant that could not die. To this end, they had the Time Squad attack the Ninth Doctor's coffin ship to capture a Vampire however the Eighth Doctor forewarned the Vampires so they could evacuate and absconded with his future self in his TARDIS. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|All Flesh is Grass (novel)}}) After he left, the Commander and Executioner received pre-recorded orders from the Emperor for event of their failure, ordering them to destroy Gallifrey before the rise of the Time Lords. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Mission to the Known (short story)}}) The Commander kept these orders secret from the Strategist and began dispatching [[Dalek scout ship|scout ships]] to eliminate the remaining Kotturuh, fearing their judgement on the Daleks. The Daleks traced one of the Vampires from the Ninth Doctor's ship, [[Ikalla]], to [[Entranxis]] where she'd been captured by the [[Death Brokers]]. A scout ship was sent to capture her, however the three Doctors were also present and helped her escape. The Daleks destroyed an oncoming Kotturuh ship and then used missiles to set Entranxis' atmosphere alight.

[[File:All Flesh Is Grass Textless.jpg|thumb|left|The [[Dalek Time Squad]] fight [[the Doctor]]s in the [[Dark Times]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|All Flesh is Grass (novel)}})]]
The Time Squad abducted a Great Vampire that was being transported aboard a coffin ship and commenced experimentation. At the same time, the Commander and Executioner alone were informed by a pre-recorded message from the Emperor of another plan, to be carried out in case of failure of the main mission - the Ultimate End: the destruction of Gallifrey in the Dark Times, before the [[Time Lord]]s had risen. Using a [[Bloodsman apparator]], the Eighth and Tenth Doctors, [[Brian (The Guide to the Dark Times)|Brian]], and a [[Geksin]], a [[Bloodsman]] from the coffin shop the Daleks had captured the Vampire from, apparated onboard the saucer, hoping to rescue the Great Vampire. The Tenth Doctor and Gelsin witnessed the creation of the Symbiont, which caused an unexpected power drain that allowed them to escape with the Eighth Doctor, while Brian chose to stay behind. Whilst escaping the Symbiont, Brian sabotaged the saucer's drive core so that, were he to be exterminated, he would take the saucer with him. Here he learned the target of the Daleks' Ultimate End and told the Doctors of it, then was rescued by the Tenth Doctor. Realising this meant that the Doctors would defend their homeworld, the Strategist ordered for Drones to be enhanced with Symbiont DNA to ensure their victory.

The Doctors came to the [[defence of Gallifrey]] in the Tenth Doctor's [[HMS Donna|flagship]], which instigated a battle between the two forces. The original Symbiont, having been sent in a scout ship to [[Birinji]] in order to exterminate the last of the Kotturuh, [[Inyit]], was judged by her and given instant death, which spread to all Drones that were given Symbiont DNA. This threw the Daleks' assault into chaos, as they panicked that the judgement may spread to pure Dalek DNA, despite the Strategist's pleas to press the attack, giving the Eighth Doctor enough time to apparate aboard the saucer and fit a trigger to the drive core that was earlier sabotaged by Brian. Using a [[Kotturuh crystal]] to amplify the blast, the resulting explosion managed to send the saucer hurling into the Time Vortex, away from the Dark Times. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|All Flesh is Grass (novel)}})

The Daleks assumed the Eighth Doctor dead, however, he had actually survived the blast using [[heat shield]]s he acquired on Atharna. He continued to sabotage the saucer, trying to disguise his work as a series of malfunctions, causing conflict between the Commander and Strategist on how to resolve the situation. The Commander favoured the Executioner, giving it autonomy to purge the ship of aliens, whilst the Strategist worked with the Scientist to stabilise the saucer. The Doctor interrupted the Scientist's work by infiltrating his laboratory and tricked him into telling him about their prisoners and secretly planted an explosive on it. He helped the prisoners escaped the Executioner's increasingly insane rampage, with it destroying a Daleks and damaging the ship in the process. The Commander was unable to rein it in, to the Strategist's frustration. The Doctor detonated his explosive, exposing half the saucer to the Vortex causing it to start to break apart. The Strategist sought out the Doctor and tried to bargain with him for safe passage in his TARDIS. He played along however exposed the deal to the Commander, resulting in a firefight between the Strategist and Commander. The Strategist prevailed, killing the Commander, which prompted the Drones to turn on him as a traitor whilst the Doctor escaped. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Mutually Assured Destruction (audio story)}})

After the saucer finally broke apart, the Time Squad was left stranded in the Time Vortex with no protection with many Drones being torn apart by [[time wind]]s. Disappointed by the failing of the Emperor's plan to destroy Gallifrey, the Strategist escaped the Time Vortex via an [[emergency temporal shift]], an ability he acquired through implementation of Kotturuh crystals into his casing. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Exit Strategy (short story)}}) One [[Dalek (The Last Message)|Drone]] survived falling through the Time Vortex, ending up adrift in space. It sent the message the Emperor had received at the start of the crisis. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Last Message (short story)}}) The Drone was eventually brought aboard the ''[[Starship Future]]'' in [[2985]]. There it attempted to rebuild its casing and encountered the [[Fourth Doctor]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Genetics of the Daleks (audio story)}}) The Restoration Empire's interaction with the Kotturuh crisis ended with the Strategist and Emperor both intent on finally making war with Gallifrey in an ultimate conflict, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Exit Strategy (short story)}}) restoring the arc of established events. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The End of Time (TV story)}}, et. al)

===== Road to the Time War =====
{{Section stub|[[The Great War (audio story)]], [[Paradox of the Daleks (audio story)]]}}
The [[Dalek Time Controller]] was saved from destruction by [[Kotris]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|X and the Daleks (audio story)}}) From then it oversaw the chasing of the Eighth Doctor and [[Molly O'Sullivan]] through time and space, ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Fugitives (audio story)|Fugitives]]'') by using a [[relativity map]] and a [[Temporal Chamber]] to create a [[Space-time projector]]. Using retro-genitor particles implanted inside Molly, it and Kotris planned to destroy the Time Lords. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Tangled Web (audio story)|Tangled Web]]'', {{cs|X and the Daleks (audio story)}}) After [[Straxus (The Great War)|Straxus]] killed himself, he erased Kotris from history. The Dalek Time Controller's plans involving Kotris were therefore erased. The Dalek Time Controller was aware of the change in history while it occurred, and swore to Kotris before he was erased that he would destroy the Time Lords. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|X and the Daleks (audio story)}})

The Dalek Time Controller oversaw the invasion of [[Nixyce VII]], and created mines in the planet to create a Dalek superweapon. The Doctor detonated a bomb located on a nearby Dalek in the time controller's chamber, damaging the Time Controller and causing him to flee to his ship in orbit above the planet. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Traitor (audio story)|The Traitor]]'') Rather than destroying the weapon, the Doctor asked for the Dalek Time Controller's help in defeating [[the Eminence]], who posed a bigger threat to the Daleks than the Doctor. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Eyes of the Master (audio story)|Eyes of the Master]]'') The Dalek Time Controller agreed, and used the weapon to destroy the Eminence fleet. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Time's Horizon (audio story)|Time's Horizon]]'')

[[File:Dark Eyes 4 no text.jpg|thumb|right|The [[Dalek Time Controller]] and other players of [[the Eminence]] crisis. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Dark Eyes 4]]'')]]
The Time Controller later arrived in [[Paris]], where it created [[Adelaine Dutemps]] from its own DNA. The controller then created [[Dalek Time Strategist]]s from the criminal minds that Adelaine dealt with. It used the power of the [[Time Vortex]] to create them. It wanted to create a new Paradigm so that it could control Daleks throughout all time. The Controller asked [[Liv Chenka]] some questions about the Eminence war, and the Doctor's involvement. The Controller opened his casing to show Liv it's eye, it was dark like Molly's. The Controller used the [[Red Pagoda]] and the TARDIS to create a larger shell. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Monster of Montmartre (audio story)|The Monster of Monmartre]]'')

The Controller travelled with {{Macqueen}} to the control centre. The Controller wanted to find [[Markus Schriver]]. The Master told the Controller that they were running out of [[human]]s to convert to Daleks so they were now using [[Sontaran]]s. The controller planed to betray the Master if the Doctor was well enough. After the Master's Dalek mutiny, he escaped with Liv and Molly in the TARDIS. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Master of the Daleks (audio story)}})

The [[Dalek Supreme (Eye of Darkness)|Dalek Supreme]] came to believe that the Controller was no longer a pure enough Dalek, having lived outside time through so many time shifts. The Supreme believed him to have been destroyed, when in actuality the Dalek Time Controller had transferred its consciousness to the gas created by [[Markus Schriver]], joining its personality with Schriver's and thus creating the Eminence. The Dalek Supreme then commissioned the creation of a new [[Dalek Time Strategist (The Shadow Vortex)|Dalek Time Strategist]] from the remains of Adelaine Dutemps. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Eye of Darkness (audio story)|Eye of Darkness]]'')

The Daleks, having readopted the [[Bronze Dalek|bronze design]] for Drones by this point, sponsored [[Free Time]], ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Ascension (Gallifrey audio story)}}) a terrorist organisation which attacked the Time Lords during [[Lord President|President]] [[Romana]]'s tenure. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Weapon of Choice (audio story)|Weapon of Choice]]'', ''[[Pandora (audio story)|Pandora]]'', ''[[Insurgency (audio story)|Insurgency]]'', ''[[Imperiatrix (audio story)|Imperiatrix]]'') After Free Time weakened the Time Lords by unleashing the [[Dogma Virus]], ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Panacea (audio story)|Panacea]]'') the Daleks invaded the [[Axis]] to plunder alternate Gallifreys, including [[Gallifrey (Forever)|one]] that Romana, [[Narvin]] and [[Leela]] from the proper timeline had settled on. The trio managed to close the Axis' portals, denying the Daleks access to anymore timelines and trapping them in any alternate timelines they had entered, and returned to Gallifrey proper. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Extermination (audio story)|Extermination]]'') The [[Supreme Dalek (Ascension)|Supreme Dalek]] led an invasion of Gallifrey via [[the Matrix]] with [[Slyne]], a resident of an alternate Gallifrey who formed an alliance with them, sent ahead to prepare for their arrival. Romana was able to trap the Daleks' invasion force in a Matrix projection with the aid of [[Romana III|a projection of her future self]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Ascension (Gallifrey audio story)}})

Dalek saucer [[X-K Beta-19]] invaded the planet [[Galacton]] to energise its core to create fuel for the [[Dalek Seventh Fleet|Seventh Fleet]]. As they drilled to the core, the Daleks were attacked by local lifeforms. In the skirmish [[Dalek Attack Squad Leader|one Dalek]] fell down the hole to the core and used its gunstick to fire on the core, sacrificing itself to achieve the Daleks' goal. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Mission to Galacton (short story)|Mission to Galacton]]'') During the [[Battle of Magella]], the [[Seventh Incursion Squad]] under a [[Dalek Commander]] wiped out the last of the [[Mechanoid]]s. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Birth of a Legend (short story)|Birth of a Legend]]'')

[[File:Father of the Daleks (short story).jpg|left|thumb|[[Davros]] and his children. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}}) ]]
The Daleks recruited [[Davros]] to lead an attack on a [[Krillitane rebels]]' base on [[Gryphon's Reach]]. However, due to the intervention of the [[Eleventh Doctor]], the Daleks were unable to destroy the base, and a number of Daleks were left behind on Gryphon's Reach. Despite Davros' claims that he could incorporate countermeasures to the Krillitanes' [[Cloaking field|cloaking technology]] into them, the Daleks abandoned Davros for his failure. Later, however, Davros convinced his children to give him another chance, offering to successfully incorporate cloaking technology into them and ambush the Doctor on [[Alacracis IV]]. Despite this, the Doctor successfully tricked the Daleks into [[self-destruct]]ing by lying to them that he could only die if Davros was killed first; at least fifty of the one-hundred Daleks attempted to exterminate Davros, triggering a failsafe system that Davros programmed into them, thereby destroying them. After the Doctor left, Davros had the remains of the Daleks transported onto [[Davros' command ship|his command ship]], so as to avoid confrontation by the rest of the [[Dalek Empire]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}})

The Daleks began attacking the [[Temporal Powers]], exterminating the [[Monan Host]], [[Sunari]] and [[Nekkistani]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Desperate Measures (audio story)|Desperate Measures]]'') After the [[Destruction of Phaidon|fall]] of [[Phaidon]], the Time Lords formally declared war on the Daleks, officially commencing the [[Last Great Time War]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Celestial Intervention (audio story)|Celestial Intervention]]'') Immediately following this, the Daleks communicated with Davros shortly after the Dalek attack on Alacracis IV, requesting his assistance in the Time War. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}})

=== The Last Great Time War ===
{{main|Last Great Time War}}
From the perspective of [[human]]ity, the Daleks vanished ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}}) after the [[Tenth Dalek Occupation]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|A Brief History of Time Lords (novel)}}) In reality, they left to fight the [[Last Great Time War]], which became known as the "final battle" between the Time Lords and the Daleks. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Dalek (TV story)}}) The Daleks were mainly commanded by the [[Dalek Emperor in the Last Great Time War|Dalek Emperor]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}}) who was guided by the [[Dalek Time Strategist (The Shadow Vortex)|Time Strategist]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Desperate Measures (audio story)|Desperate Measures]]'') The Daleks committed "untold" crimes over the course of the War. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Wanted! Daleks (feature)}}) The Time War also saw the creation of many new Dalek variants of questionable purity, from the [[Skaro Degradations]] ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Engines of War (novel)}}) to secret societies of Daleks with increased creativity, placed beyond the control of the Emperor, such as the [[Cult of Skaro]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|Doomsday (TV story)}}) and the [[Volatix Cabal]]. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[Downtime (comic story)|Downtime]]'', ''[[The Organ Grinder (comic story)|The Organ Grinder]]'' et al.)

In the first year of the Time War, Davros was asked by the Emperor to make a new creature for use against the Time Lords, promising him acceptance and his own legion. The result was the [[Nightmare Child]]. The Child quickly went out of control, wanting to consume everything, so Davros lured it to the [[Gates of Elysium]] to destroy it. With him aboard, his command ship was swallowed by the Child as it fell into the Gates. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Third Wise Man (short story)}}) Davros was believed dead. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}})

[[File:Soldier Obscura textless.jpg|thumb|Daleks, [[Ace]], and [[Irving Braxiatel]] on [[the Obscura]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Soldier Obscura (audio story)}})]]
Early in the war, a Dalek ship received a call telling them that a cache of Gallifreyan weapons was being hidden at a station in [[the Obscura]]. When the fleet arrived, they discovered it was a trap by [[Irving Braxiatel]], who wanted [[Danna]] to use her skills to destroy them. Danna was unable to fulfil his trap, so Braxiatel was forced to expose the station to the Obscura to destroy the Daleks. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Soldier Obscura (audio story)}})

After undoing his scheme to rewrite time by replacing Davros as the Daleks' creator, the Time Strategist ordered the Daleks to capture {{Jacobi}}. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|He Who Wins (audio story)}}) They bombarded [[The Master's TARDIS|his TARDIS]] and extracted him by transmat beam. He agreed to work for them in return for allowing him to retrieve his TARDIS from where it had crashed, the Dalek-occupied world of [[Gardezza]]. He ultimately betrayed them, using the damage to his TARDIS to destroy the Dalek saucer occupying the planet. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Beneath the Viscoid (audio story)|Beneath the Viscoid]]'') The Daleks continued to pursue him, following him to [[Arcking]]. The Daleks invaded the planet, having to utilise unusual methods due to its state of [[temporal grace]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Good Master (audio story)|The Good Master]]'')

Two months into the War, the Daleks discovered [[Project Revenant]], a [[War Council]] facility that was resurrecting Time Lords, and launched an invasion of its pocket dimension. During this time, [[Celestial Intervention Agency|CIA]] Coordinator [[Romana]] opened secret negotiations with the Emperor, unsuccessfully attempting to convince him to end the War. The CIA prevented the Daleks capturing Project Revenant by arranging its destruction just as they boarded the facility. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Desperate Measures (audio story)|Desperate Measures]]'')

The Daleks pursued Time Lord agent [[Aymor]] in his search for [[Quarren Maguire|an erased superweapon]], following him to the starship ''Theseus ''which they boarded. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Starship of Theseus (audio story)|The Starship of Theseus]]'') Cardinal [[War Ollistra|Ollistra]] subsequently lured a Dalek fleet to a trap at the planet where the ''Theseus'' crashed. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Echoes of War (audio story)}}) The Daleks attacked the [[Gallifreyan Military Moon Base|Time Lord facility]] on the [[Moon of Tenacity]], deploying a reversal wave through the [[Tenacity system|Tenacity System]] to erase its defences. They pursued the Doctor's TARDIS from Tenacity, battling a Time Lord fleet over [[Jedris]] where it eventually crashed. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Conscript (audio story)|The Conscript]]'', ''[[One Life (audio story)|One Life]]'')

After being alerted by an agent that the Time Lords had occupied it and were building an arsenal of rockets, the Daleks invaded [[Derilobia]]. They captured Commander [[Carvil]]'s [[Carvil's TARDIS|TARDIS]], however it self-destructed after he was exterminated and the distraction it caused enabled the Time Lord forces to evacuate. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Lords of Terror (audio story)|The Lords of Terror]]'')

A Dalek force led by [[the Overseer]] occupied [[The Planet]] and enslaved the Ogrons. The Overseer conducted numerous experiments on the Ogrons, including retrospectively adding them to past Dalek battles. When the Doctor and [[the Twelve]] investigated the Planet, the Overseer created [[Doctor Ogron]] by mixing the Doctor with an Ogron. Doctor Ogron led a revolt against the Daleks, during which a task force arrived to relieve the Overseer of command as its experiments had been deemed an abomination to Dalek purity. The Doctor, the Twelve and Bliss were also captured ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Planet of the Ogrons (audio story)|Planet of the Ogrons]]'') and taken to a prison camp on [[Sangrey]] for interrogation, though they managed to escape. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[In the Garden of Death (audio story)|In the Garden of Death]]'') Based on information from the Twelve's interrogation, the [[Admiral (Jonah)|Admiral]] led a Dalek expedition to [[Uzmal]] to find the legendary [[Ourashima]]. Battling resistance forces led by the Doctor and Ollistra, the Daleks found the Ourashima but were unable to communicate with it. To prevent it falling into the Time Lords' hands, the Admiral sacrificed the entire taskforce to kill it. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Jonah (audio story)|Jonah]]'')

[[File:Dalek Time Strategist (Fugitive in Time).jpeg|left|thumb|The [[Dalek Time Strategist]] on [[Thellian]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Fugitive in Time (audio story)}})]]
The Dalek Time Strategist led a Dalek mission to [[Thellian]] to acquire a genetic modifier created by [[Shonnath]], the last of the [[Helixara]], that she had used to prevent herself from being erased from [[history]] by the Time Lords. The Daleks were unable to land on the planet, so sent [[Vashko (Dalek duplicate)|a duplicate]] first who arranged for them to transmat down. The Eighth Doctor, Bliss and the [[Sixth Tamasan]] beat the Daleks to the genetic modifier and escaped with it. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Fugitive in Time (audio story)}})

The Daleks, with the exception of the Time Strategist which escaped through a rift, were erased from history by [[the Valeyard]] who turned their own superweapon against them on [[Grahv]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The War Valeyard (audio story)|The War Valeyard]]'') The Time Strategist used dimensional engineering and a [[Davros (Palindrome)|parallel universe version of Davros]] to restore the Daleks. The simulacra Davros attempted to assert his authority over the Daleks, however the Strategist arranged the restoration of the Emperor. The Emperor had the simulacra put in stasis, believing he may be of use one day. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Palindrome (audio story)|Palindrome]]'', {{cs|Restoration of the Daleks (audio story)}})

The Daleks employed a [[Time Destructor]] in order to gain the upper hand in the war, destroying [[Polymos]] and creating a temporal shockwave which affected systems from the [[Farflung Rift]] to the [[Wolf's Heart Nebula]]. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Natural Regression (short story)|Natural Regression]]'')

A skirmish between Dalek and Time Lord forces devastated the planet [[Drakkis]] throughout its history. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Sontaran Ordeal (audio story)|The Sontaran Ordeal]]'')

The Daleks began feeding the Time Lords intelligence in order to lure them into an ambush on Skaro. Their plan succeeded, with a fleet of [[Battle TARDIS]]es assaulting Skaro, only to fall victim to a new Dalek superweapon. However, the [[War Doctor]] and [[Petrella]] survived the ambush and were able to warn the Time Lords of the Dalek superweapon. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[Ambush (comic story)|Ambush]]'')

The Daleks had dealings with a crime boss, [[Jarred McKenzie]], on [[Unity]]. He revealed he had found a [[TARDIS (Assassins)|TARDIS]], prompting the Daleks to invade the planet fully to exterminate the Time Lords it belonged to. They found Romana alone and attempted to exterminate her ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Unity (audio story)|Unity]]'') however she was saved by [[Irving Braxiatel]]. The Daleks pursued her associates, including [[Narvin]], to a resistance base which they attacked. A [[Hunter Dalek]] subsequently followed Narvin to [[Micallon]] but failed to capture him. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Dissolution (audio story)|Dissolution]]'') Romana was later captured when the Daleks ambushed Braxiatel's TARDIS. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Homecoming (audio story)|Homecoming]]'')

The Dalek Emperor and Time Strategist launched a gambit to seize Gallifrey using null zone technology. Their saucer easily bypassed Kasteroborus' defences using this method but required time to recharge to land on Gallifrey. During this time, the Daleks fended off Time Lord counterattacks using the null zone technology and used Romana as a spokesperson to the Time Lords.
