Their plan failed when Narvin and [[War Livia Caralis]] detonated a Battle TARDIS by the null zone power source, with the Emperor and Strategist escaping before the saucer was destroyed. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Homecoming (audio story)|Homecoming]]'')

During the year [[A10%?]], the Daleks attacked [[Marinus]]. Working with the [[Voord]], the War Doctor defended the planet with a [[chronic tripwire]], which aged the Daleks in an attacking [[Dalek ship (Four Doctors)|flying saucer]] to dust. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Four Doctors (comic story)}})

Late in the War, the Daleks assembled a huge fleet of timeships to invade Gallifrey. The fleet was intercepted by the Time Lords, who deployed a [[Time Destructor]] to annihilate it. The War Doctor replaced the assigned Time Lords and fired it himself, barely escaping with his life. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Innocent (audio story)|The Innocent]]'')

A Dalek agent, [[Lara Zannis]], breached the time lock around Earth, arriving in 1961 Berlin, pursued by the War Doctor. She used the [[Shadow Vortex]] to enable the Time Strategist to invade Earth. The Daleks hoped to rewrite history by preventing the Doctor's companions existing, however the War Doctor un-did the invasion by using his TARDIS to collide the Shadow Vortex with its past self pre-activation, erasing Lara in the process. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Shadow Vortex (audio story)|The Shadow Vortex]]'')

The Dalek Time Strategist was captured by Sontarans seeking to join the Time War led by [[Fesk]]. He was held captive with Cardinal Ollistra on [[Rovidia]], with the Daleks unable to rescue him due to the Sontarans' temporal defences powered by the [[Eternity Cage]]. The War Doctor infiltrated Rovidia and deactivated the Cage, which enabled the Daleks in orbit to descend on the planet. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Eternity Cage (audio story)|The Eternity Cage]]'') Whilst the Daleks destroyed the Rovidian fleet, the Time Strategist took the opportunity to order a Dalek agent, [[Heleyna]], who was onboard the TARDIS that the Doctor and Ollistra had escaped in, to use the Cardinal to open that TARDIS' link to the Eye of Harmony. A Dalek Assault Squad was sent to use the link to reach Gallifrey, however the Doctor used the TARDIS' reconfiguration system to delete the Eye of Harmony chamber, wiping them out. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Eye of Harmony (audio story)|Eye of Harmony]]'') The Time Strategist subsequently led a fleet in pursuit of the Doctor and Ollistra, first to a space station and then to [[Beltox]]. Their initial assault on Beltox was defeated, enabling the Doctor and Ollistra to escape again, however the Daleks returned and destroyed the planet. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Pretty Lies (audio story)|Pretty Lies]]'') The Daleks followed them to [[Grend]], where their invasion was defeated by a squadron of Battle TARDISes and the forces of the Lady of Obsidian, Leela. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Lady of Obsidian (audio story)|The Lady of Obsidian]]'')

The Time Strategist made contact with [[the Enigma]], a being from another dimension, and convinced it to erase the Time Lords, turning Gallifrey into a Dalek world. The Enigma had doubts however so reverted things back shortly afterwards, and was finally convinced by the War Doctor, Ollistra and Leela to stay out of the War. It expelled all the Daleks in its dimension. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Enigma Dimension (audio story)|The Enigma Dimension]]'')

Several Daleks from late in the War travelled back in time to attack a munitions factory in the [[Mountain of Serenity]] where Gallifreyan children were being kept safe, with the intent of killing them before they could take part in the War. The War Doctor evacuated the children, and [[Tahl]] sacrificed himself by detonating explosives in the mountain, causing a collapse that buried the Daleks. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Stranger (short story)}})

At one point, the Daleks managed to amass an enormous fleet and launch an overwhelming assault on Gallifrey. Facing annihilation, and with no other options left, [[Lord Cardinal|Cardinal]] Ollistra had [[Councillor]] [[Voltrix]] open a rift in [[space]], releasing the [[Great Vampire]]s, which destroyed the Dalek fleet. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[The Bidding War (comic story)|The Bidding War]]'')

[[File:Fall of Arcadia begins.jpg|right|thumb|[[Dalek drone]]s begin the [[Fall of Arcadia]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Last Day (TV story)}})]]
On the [[Fall of Gallifrey|last day of the Time War]], the Daleks broke the defences of [[Arcadia (city)|Arcadia]], Gallifrey's second city, ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Last Day (TV story)}}) and [[Fall of Arcadia|invaded it]]. Unable to to breach the [[Capitol]]'s [[sky trench]]es, the Dalek fleet surrounded and bombarded Gallifrey. The War Doctor planned to use a weapon known as [[the Moment]] to wipe out both the Time Lords and the Daleks. However, this option was not taken, and "all thirteen" incarnations of the Doctor teamed up together to hide Gallifrey and the Time Lords in an unknown [[pocket universe]], leaving the Dalek fleet to wipe itself out in its own crossfire. In outward appearances, the result of this action was the same as if the Moment had been used: Gallifrey disappeared and the Daleks were (mostly) destroyed. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Day of the Doctor (TV story)}})

=== Surviving the Time War ===
[[File:Genesis Ark opened.jpg|left|thumb|Daleks escape the Genesis Ark. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Doomsday (TV story)}})]]
The [[Ninth Doctor]] incorrectly assumed that "the entire Dalek race" had been "wiped out" by the Time War. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Dalek (TV story)}}) There were, however, numerous exceptions.

==== Runaways ====
In his book on the end of the Last Great Time War, the Doctor's future incarnation [[the Curator]] acknowledged the unlikelihood of so few Daleks as later encountered by the Doctor having survived the blast that ended the Time War, no matter how great an explosion that was. He stated that his personal belief was that upon witnessing, at the moment of what should have been their final victory, the skies of [[Gallifrey]] being filled with a veritable swarm of versions of their worst enemy [[the Doctor]], most of the Daleks who did not die were struck with such unimaginable amounts of [[fear]] that they ran way in terror to parts unknown, and were "probably still running now". ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Day of the Doctor (novelisation)}})

==== Scattered survivors ====
The first of the Time War survivor Daleks encountered by the Doctor fell through time and crashed like a [[meteorite]] "on the [[Ascension Islands]]". The Dalek lay in its burning crater for three days, screaming the entire time, before it was retrieved. Its weapon systems inactive and its outer armour heavily damaged, the Dalek was sold at private auction and passed through several hands over the next fifty years. In [[2012]] it was acquired by billionaire [[Henry Van Statten]] who nicknamed it [[Metaltron]]. It sent a distress signal to the [[Ninth Doctor]] and his companion [[Rose Tyler]]. Upon Rose's touch it absorbed a small amount of her DNA, using the [[artron energy]] of a time traveller's DNA to revivify itself. Breaking out of confinement, it went on a rampage, only to realise that its absorbing Rose's DNA had caused it to begin mutating into "something different... something new", a Dalek-human hybrid with the swirling thoughts and emotions, and the reluctance to kill, of a [[human]]. Refusing to become impure, and unable to cope with the independence of mind that was coming to it, it ultimately [[Suicide|self-destructed]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Dalek (TV story)}})

Toward the end of the [[Last Great Time War]] the Daleks sent a [[time capsule]] to [[70]] [[AD]] [[Earth]] in order to spread the [[Dalek Factor]] amongst the humans to use humans to build more Daleks as back-up for the Time War. The capsule's engine failed during the trip and the Dalek inside ejected, crashing on Earth. It died shortly thereafter and released only a small amount of the Dalek Factor, leading to only one in five hundred million humans having it. The [[Tenth Doctor]] discovered the dead shell which had been a Roman exhibit until the British threw it into some caves and gave the Dalek gunstick to [[Frank Openshaw]]. However, the unearthing of the Dalek activated the Dalek Factor in [[Kate Yates]] who developed a Dalek personality and touched the dead casing, causing her Dalek life-force to grow a new Dalek in the casing from the casing's databanks. The Dalek hunted down Frank and killed him to retrieve its gun arm and then went on a rampage, killing many people before finding Kate. When the Doctor arrived, the Dalek offered the Doctor a deal: if he gave it a way to travel in time and space, it would spare Earth and go to another planet to rebuild its race and spread across the universe. If the Doctor refused, it would destroy the Earth. With no way to destroy the Dalek, the Doctor agreed to the deal and provided it with [[Time Ring (I Am a Dalek)|an old Time Ring]] he had stored in the TARDIS. The Dalek revealed its plan to be to travel to the year 500 million where humanity was peaceful and had no knowledge of the Daleks. There he'd get Kate to convince the humans to give it the materials it needed to rebuild its race. As the Dalek prepared to exterminate the Doctor, Rose reached out to Kate's human side, trying to get her to fight her Dalek side by reminding her of the [[good]] of humanity. After a mental struggle, Kate's human side regained control and she used her Dalek knowledge to set the Time Ring to self-destruct. The Dalek, trapped by Kate in a force field to protect the Doctor during her mental struggle, was caught in a warp implosion caused by the Time Ring self-destructing and was atomised. The Dalek Factor in Kate then deactivated without the Dalek there to stir it up and she lost everything the Dalek Factor had given her including her increased intelligence and Dalek personality. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|I Am a Dalek (novel)}})

A group of surviving Daleks unleashed their [[proton cannon]] on [[22nd century]] Earth, resulting in all life becoming intangible (unable to touch solids). The plan was that, unable to eat, humans would soon just waste away from the Earth and the Dalek survivors would rebuild war ships and attack. The Tenth Doctor used the [[Krikoosh]] to reach the proton cannon. Unhurt by the Daleks' rays, the Doctor made some adjustments and turned the weapon against the Daleks. The humans became solid again and the Daleks with their 'protective' shields were left intangible. The Daleks judged this an unacceptable outcome and [[self-destruct]]ed. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[Extermination of the Daleks (comic story)|Extermination of the Daleks]]'')

[[Dalek (Hell Bent)|One Dalek]], trapped in [[the Matrix]] under Gallifrey, was encountered by the [[Twelfth Doctor]] after Gallifrey's restoration. The Doctor speculated it had been there since the [[Cloister Wars]]. It begged to be exterminated when it was ensnared by the [[Cloister Wraith]]s. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Hell Bent (TV story)}})

==== The Dalek Emperor's "long game" ====
[[File:Parting-dalekemperor.jpg|thumb|The [[Dalek Emperor (The Parting of the Ways)|Dalek Emperor]] surrounded by his loyal worshippers as his plan reaches fruition. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}}]]
The [[Dalek Emperor in the Last Great Time War|Dalek Emperor]] barely survived the "inferno", and fell through time in his damaged [[Dalek Flagship|flagship]]. Damaged, but rebuilding slowly, the Emperor influenced the [[Fourth Great and Bountiful Human Empire]] as a cover for his plans. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}}) He used the [[Jagrafess]] and [[the Editor]] as puppets in circa 199,909. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Long Game (TV story)}}, {{cs|Bad Wolf (TV story)}}) It rebuilt the Dalek race [[Dalek of human origin|using human cells]] to create an army of just about half a million Daleks. It also built 200 [[Dalek flying saucer|flying saucers]] containing more than 2000 Daleks each. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Bad Wolf (TV story)}}) The Emperor, having recreated the Dalek race, saw itself as an immortal god, and so was literally worshipped by the new Daleks. These and other religious concepts such as blasphemy were new to Dalek psychology. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}})

The Emperor's pawn, [[Controller (Bad Wolf)|the Controller]], hated her masters and [[transmat]]ted the Ninth Doctor and his allies to the [[Satellite Five|Game Station]] to help defeat them. When he discovered the fleet and the new Daleks, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Bad Wolf (TV story)}}) the Doctor realised that the Daleks hated their own existence since they were partially human. Additionally, they had been driven mad by hundreds of years of solitude. [[Jack Harkness]] led a small human resistance to stop the Daleks. Thanks to [[Rodrick]], the humans on [[Floor 000]] didn't help him. On [[Floor 500]] The Doctor decided to create a [[Delta Wave]] to destroy the Daleks, but didn't have enough time to refine it so that it could distinguish between humans and Daleks. The Doctor decided to turn his chance down to use the delta wave to kill humans and Daleks alike, even though the Daleks had just bombed Earth heavily, wiping out entire continents. The Emperor thought he was victorious, but he and his entire fleet were atomised by Rose Tyler after she had absorbed the energies of the time vortex and became the [[Bad Wolf (entity)|Bad Wolf]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}})

==== Schemes of the Cult of Skaro ====
The [[Cult of Skaro]] had been created by the [[Dalek Emperor]] and were given names. [[Dalek Sec]] was the leader of the cult, and the others were named [[Dalek Caan]], [[Dalek Thay]] and [[Dalek Jast]]. They were "above and beyond the Emperor himself" and were designed to "think as the enemy thinks" and to imagine new ways of survival as well as new ways of killing. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Doomsday (TV story)}}) By one account, the Cult was formed before the Time War and were just four ordinary Daleks originally. Dalek Sec was the [[Dalek Commander]] of the [[Seventh Incursion Squad]] sent to wipe out the remnants of the [[Mechanoid]]s on [[Magella]] which they succeeded in doing. Dalek Caan was an [[Attack Squad Leader]] of the [[Thirtieth Assault Group]]. Dalek Thay was the [[Commandant]] of [[Station Alpha]], the most secret Dalek research facility. Dalek Jast was the [[Force Leader]] of the [[Outer Rim Defensive Battalion]]. After doing this, they were promoted to become the Cult of Skaro. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Birth of a Legend (short story)|Birth of a Legend]]'') A group of researchers later claimed the Cult had been formed during the war. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}})

[[File:Cult of Skaro.jpg|thumb|The Cult of Skaro. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Doomsday (TV story)}})|alt=|left]]The Cult, foreseeing a disastrous end on the Daleks' side by the end of the Time War, built a [[Void Ship]] for themselves, which allowed them to hide away outside the universe, in [[the Void]] between parallel realities. They had acquired a Time Lord prison ship, the ''[[Genesis Ark]]'', which contained millions of Daleks captured during the war. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Doomsday (TV story)}}) They leaked back into 21st century Earth, inadvertently allowing five million [[Cyberman|Cybermen]] from [[Pete's World|a parallel world]] to follow in the "wake" of their Void Ship and invade the Earth. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Army of Ghosts (TV story)}}) After emerging from the Void Ship, the Cult held [[Rose Tyler]] and [[Mickey Smith]] hostage while Dalek Thay confronted the Cybermen. Thay turned down an offer of an alliance from the Cybermen, prompting the [[Cyber-Leader (Pete's World)|Cyber-leader]] to declare war on the Daleks, while the Cult, confident in the ability of even one Dalek to destroy the "inferior" species, stated that he deemed the wiping out of the Cybermen to be nothing more than "pest control".

Sec then oversaw the pulling of the ''Ark'' out of hibernation with the touch of a time traveller, allowing the liberated Daleks to fight the Cybermen (as well as human [[Torchwood One]] personnel) for dominion over the Earth in the [[Battle of Canary Wharf]]. Through the efforts of the [[Tenth Doctor]], however, the majority of these Daleks were sucked back into the Void, with the only the four members of the Cult of Skaro themselves managing to escape through an [[Temporal shift|emergency temporal shift]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Doomsday (TV story)}})

The Cult emerged in [[1930]] in [[New York City]], where their first concern was to breed new [[Mutant Dalek embryo|Dalek embryos]]. However, they soon abandoned them to die in the sewers, as "their flesh was too weak". This failure led Dalek Sec to determine that the Daleks' obsession with purity and supremacy had brought them to near-extinction, and that the only way for the Daleks to survive was by forcing them to evolve. Sec thus created the [[Human-Dalek]]s, even going so far as to splice his own body with that of a human ally of theirs, [[Diagoras|Mr Diagoras]]. To do so, the Cult infiltrated the construction of the [[Empire State Building]] and set up a [[Transgenic Laboratory]] beneath it, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Daleks in Manhattan (TV story)}}) from which they planned to use [[Dalekanium]] placed on the mast as an energy conductor for [[gamma radiation]] from a [[solar flare]] to power the [[Final Experiment]].

Despite the arrival of the Tenth Doctor and [[Martha Jones]], the Daleks' [[Invasion of Manhattan]] began to unfold, only for Sec's new human emotions to begin to change his vision for their plans. The other three Daleks ruled that Sec had gone too far and had betrayed the Dalek ethos; they stripped him of his authority and eventually killed him. Their attempt to make an army out of Sec's Dalek-Humans was foiled by the Tenth Doctor and [[Martha Jones]], after the Doctor had agreed to work with Sec to make the kidnapped humans in the Experiment into hybrids that were even more humanlike than Sec. Sec sacrificed himself to save the Doctor's life from Thay, Jast and Caan, who then ordered their Dalek-Humans to take aim at him. The hybrids, however, questioned their orders and refused to fire. The Doctor revealed that his getting in the way of the lightning-strike had caused his [[Time Lord]] DNA to mix with the human-Daleks and that gave them freedom. Still stunned, Thay and Jast killed a few human-Daleks but were killed in the process. Caan, declaring the Human-Daleks a "failure", exterminated the new species. The Doctor confronted Caan and offered help, claiming not wanting to cause another [[genocide]] after seeing one already, but Caan once again used a temporal shift to escape. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Evolution of the Daleks (TV story)}})

Caan, seeing no better way to bring the Dalek race back to its former glory, broke the [[time lock]] on the [[Last Great Time War]] to rescue Davros from the jaws of the [[Nightmare Child]]. Davros then used his own body cells to recreate the Dalek race and rebuilt a [[Dalek Fleet]] of two hundred ships. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}})

=== Creation and destruction of the New Dalek Empire ===
[[File:Daleks are the masters of Earth.jpg|thumb|right|The Daleks are the masters of Earth. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}})]]
The planet-sized station known as the [[Crucible]] was the flagship of the [[New Dalek Empire]]. The [[Supreme Dalek (The Stolen Earth)|Supreme Dalek]] was created and locked Davros and Caan inside [[The Vault (The Stolen Earth)|the Vault]] while guarded by [[Vault Dalek]]s. The new fully-formed Empire [[Stolen planets|transported 27 planets]] to the [[Medusa Cascade]] and took control over the planets. In their attack on Earth, they took many humans aboard their ships, and wiped out any resistance that they met. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}}) During the [[21st century Dalek invasion|Dalek invasion]], a [[Dalek (The Waters of Mars)|Dalek]] was observed by a young [[Adelaide Brooke]] as it passed by her house. This Dalek spared her life, flying off to space. This inspired her to go to space, not for revenge, but to explore. The [[Tenth Doctor]] believed it recognised her as a [[Fixed point|fixed point in time]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Waters of Mars (TV story)}})

The new Empire planned to use the 27 planets in conjunction with the Crucible's energy source to power a [[reality bomb]] created by Davros who intend to make the destruction of all existence and allow the Daleks to be the sole inhabitants and masters of the universe. The Supreme Dalek made an arrangement with Davros; the creator of the Daleks would ensure their domination of the universe if they allowed him to live. The plan failed by the interference of the [[Donna Noble|DoctorDonna]], who closed off all of the [[Z-Neutrino]] energy relay loops of the reality bomb by using an [[internalised synchronous back-feed reversal loop]], locked the Daleks' weaponry in a [[self-replicating energy blindfold matrix]] through [[macrotransmission of a K-filter wavelength]] and interfered with the Daleks' systems with a [[trip stitch circuit-breaker]] in the [[psycho-kinetic threshold manipulator]].

Deciding the Dalek Empire was a threat too great for the universe, the [[Meta-Crisis Tenth Doctor]] maximised the [[Dalekanium]] [[Dalekanium power feed|power feeds]] and blasted them back, executing every Dalek around them and destroying the entire fleet. The destruction of the Void by the reality bomb, which through Donna and the Meta-Crisis Doctor's interference, was reversed through [[dimensional retroclosure]], ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}}) though the Daleks who were sucked into [[the Void]] were still be destroyed, with only a handful of [[Cyberman|Cybermen]] being able to escape with stolen Dalek technology like the [[Dimension Vault]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Next Doctor (TV story)}}) [[Rose Tyler]] claimed that "even the Void was dead", ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}}) while the Tenth Doctor said that a "greater battle" than [[Battle of Canary Wharf|the one]] that locked the Daleks and Cybermen into the Void rose up, which was "so great that everything inside the Void perished". ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Next Doctor (TV story)}})

=== The New Dalek Paradigm ===
==== The restoration of the Daleks ====
[[File:Victory of the daleks.jpg|thumb|left|The [[Eleventh Doctor]] faces the new legion of Daleks. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Victory of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
A trio of drones from the New Dalek Empire, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}) survived its fall in their [[Dalek flying saucer|flying saucer]], falling through time to [[1941]].

There, the trio picked up the trace of the last surviving [[Progenitor]], which contained pure Dalek DNA, which they intended to create new Daleks with which to restore their race. However, as their DNA was so mangled as to be "unrecognisable as Dalek" to the Progenitor, they were forced to start a scheme called the [[Ironside Project]] and created an android named [[Edwin Bracewell]] to claim they were his inventions and two of the three Daleks pretended to be ironsides for the [[British Army]] during [[World War II]] to ensure [[Winston Churchill]] would contact the [[Eleventh Doctor]] to trick him into delivering his testimony to the Progenitor. Despite their cover blown, the Daleks successfully obtained the Doctor's testimony and returned to their ship to commence their plan. The Doctor used a [[Jammie Dodger]] to fool them into thinking it was a [[TARDIS self-destruct]]. To counter this, the Daleks activated a beacon to turn the lights of London on to allow German bombers to destroy the city. Five new, larger Daleks were created, with pure DNA and a new colour-coded rank. The Supreme Dalek told the old Daleks they were impure, which they accepted and they allowed themselves to be disintegrated with no resistance. The new Daleks discovered the Doctor's deception and that the TARDIS self-destruct was fake. The Doctor told [[Danny Boy (Victory of the Daleks)|Danny Boy]] to destroy the ship after he destroyed the beacon. The Daleks threatened to destroy the [[Earth]] with the [[Oblivion Continuum]] inside Bracewell unless the Doctor called off his attack. He complied and returned to Earth to disarm the bomb. After the bomb was disarmed, the new Daleks escaped in a time corridor to rebuild their empire based on the [[New Dalek Paradigm]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Victory of the Daleks (TV story)}})

Following their escape, the Daleks discovered the lost Time Lord artefact, the [[Eye of Harmony|Eye of Time]], allowing them to alter time as they saw fit. The Daleks returned to [[Skaro]], rebuilt their capital city of [[Kaalann]], appointed a new [[Dalek Emperor]] and began rebuilding their Empire. In this new timeline, they killed every member of the [[human]] race. However, the Eleventh Doctor and Amy undid these events, leaving Earth unconquered and Kaalann still abandoned. ([[GAME]]: {{cs|City of the Daleks (video game)}})

==== Plaguing the universe once more ====
The [[Supreme Dalek (Return to Earth)|Dalek Supreme]] led an attack on the ''[[SS Lucy Gray]]'' to recover the Daleks' lost [[Time Axis]]. The Eleventh Doctor defeated them by firing their ship into the [[sun]]. ([[GAME]]: {{cs|Return to Earth (video game)}}) The Dalek ship escaped by making a random jump several hundred years into the past. The Daleks attempted to force the Doctor to fix their ship by attaching [[The Doctor's TARDIS|his TARDIS]] to their ship; the Doctor escaped and used his TARDIS to fling their ship into a [[black hole]]. ([[GAME]]: {{cs|Evacuation Earth (video game)}})

A [[Scientist Dalek (The Mazes of Time)|Scientist Dalek]] sent an alien family plummeting through time and space to collect all the [[Time orb]]s. The Scientist recruited many [[Strategist Dalek|Strategist]] Daleks and [[Drone Dalek|Drones]]. It also recruited big armies of [[Cyberman|Cybermen]] and [[Silurian]]s as a distraction for the [[Eleventh Doctor]] and [[Amy Pond|Amy]]. ([[GAME]]: {{cs|The Mazes of Time (video game)}})

[[File:Chief Strategist and subordinates.jpg|thumb|The [[Chief Strategist]] during the 41st century [[War (The Only Good Dalek)|war with humanity]]. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|The Only Good Dalek (comic story)}})]]
At the beginning of the [[40th century]], the Daleks began [[War (The Only Good Dalek)|another war with humanity]] which continued into the [[41st century]]. The Eleventh Doctor and Amy encountered a group led by the [[Chief Strategist]] who had been sent on a mission to find a Dalek mutant being experimented on by [[Weston (The Only Good Dalek)|a scientist]] who tried to make them less aggressive creatures. The Daleks referred to this mutant as [[The Abomination (The Only Good Dalek)|"the Abomination"]]. They attacked and destroyed Earth's top secret space station, [[Station 7]], and chased the survivors to the planet [[Strantana]] below. After slaughtering all resistance, they finally found the Abomination in a hidden base, but it escaped its container and disabled the base reactor's safety measures.

An explosion destroyed the base, the Daleks, and all the Dalek ships that had landed on the planet. The Doctor, Amy and [[Jay Bourne|Jay]], an [[Space Security Service|SSS]] officer, watched from a safe distance. The Dalek mission was a failure but the war continued. They had agents working in the SSS. The Abomination secretly survived the explosion, but the Doctor remained certain there was no such thing as a good Dalek. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|The Only Good Dalek (comic story)}})

The Daleks joined the [[Pandorica Alliance]] to imprison the Eleventh Doctor in the [[Pandorica]] in [[102]] to save the [[universe]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Pandorica Opens (TV story)}}) As the Doctor was not responsible for the [[Total Event Collapse]] as they thought, the Daleks, along with almost the rest of the universe, were destroyed, leaving only two [[Stone Dalek]]s, one of which hindered the Doctor and his companions' efforts to save the universe in [[1996]]. Nevertheless, they were successful and the whole of reality, including the Daleks, were restored. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Big Bang (TV story)}})

The Doctor had an encounter with the Daleks during which they exterminated [[Albert Einstein]]'s [[toothbrush]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Death Is the Only Answer (TV story)}})

[[File:Hello Dalek.jpg|thumb|left|The [[Eleventh Doctor]] confronts a wrecked [[Supreme Dalek (The Wedding of River Song)|Dalek Supreme]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Wedding of River Song (TV story)}})]]
Searching for information on the Silence before going to what he assumed was his death, the Doctor found a badly damaged [[Dalek (The Wedding of River Song)|Supreme Dalek]] and used it to look up information on [[the Silence]]. Shortly afterward, the Doctor was seemingly killed at [[Lake Silencio]] in [[2011]], ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Wedding of River Song (TV story)}}) but the Daleks, correctly, believed their foe was still alive. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Asylum of the Daleks (TV story)}}) {{Gomez}} claimed that a Dalek learned of the Doctor's supposed death from a [[Order of the Headless|Headless Monk]] and then told a [[Draconian]], who then told her. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Bekdel Test (audio story)|The Bekdel Test]]'')

==== A new Emperor ====
Led by a new [[Emperor Dalek (City of the Daleks)|Emperor Dalek]], the Daleks planned to remove [[Gallifrey]] from existence and become the new [[Time Lord|Lords of Time]]. They used a piece of the [[Eternity Clock]] to put a time lock around a large part of [[London]] in [[2106]]. Once they perfected their time lock technology, they planned to use it to put temporal bubbles around other planets, making them unstoppable. The [[Eleventh Doctor]] and [[River Song]] infiltrated the [[Dalek Flagship|Emperor's Flagship]] and managed to take back the piece of the Clock. ([[GAME]]: {{cs|The Eternity Clock (video game)}})

During the reign of the New Paradigm, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}) a small contingent of bronze Daleks were sent on a mission to travel through [[Earth]]'s history and analyse how [[human]]s made war so that weaknesses could be found and exploited in future conflicts with the Daleks. They called this the [[Dalek Project]]. The Eleventh Doctor encountered these Daleks in the [[First World War]] in [[1917]] where he sent their [[Dalek flying saucer|ship]] crashing to the ground by ramming a plane into it. The remaining Daleks were destroyed by the combined armies of the war who had formed a very brief alliance to defend themselves. The Dalek saucer remained underground for [[2017|one hundred years]] before it was found and accidentally reactivated by a team of [[archaeologist]]s. The Eleventh Doctor arrived in time to save them and connected the ship up to a power line, overloading the Daleks. He called this "unfinished business". ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|The Dalek Project (comic story)}})

==== The Cradle of the Gods ====
At a point where the New Paradigm was relying heavily on bronze casings, the New Paradigm discovered the superweapon known as the [[Cradle of the Gods]] and learned of its ability to create or destroy on a massive scale. To make use of the weapon, the Daleks used a huge galactic recession to their advantage and created 400 [[planet]]s to provide homes to the billions of people affected, which were collectively referred to as the [[Sunlight Worlds]]. It was governed by the [[Dalek Foundation]], with the planet [[Carthedia]] of the [[Earth Alliance]] acting as a head of state. While a generation of people believed the Daleks had created a welfare state, it was in fact a plan headed by the [[Dalek Time Controller]] and the [[Dalek Supreme]] to transform the 400 worlds into copies of [[Skaro]].

However, the Daleks were unable to activate the Cradle and so they sent an anonymous message in the form of a [[hypercube]] to [[the Doctor's TARDIS]] with the intention of manipulating him into activating the Cradle instead. The Doctor's investigations resulted in shock when he learned the Daleks were considered a force for [[good]] and he was placed on trial while trying to convince the citizens of Carthedia that they were [[evil]], which the Daleks had declared a [[hate crime]]. He was put on trial by the Dalek Litigator, who was really the Dalek Time Controller posing as a law enforcer, and when he pleaded guilty in a failed attempt to anger the Dalek and was sentenced to imprisonment, he escaped off-planet with three orphaned children, [[Sabel Blakely|Sabel]], [[Jenibeth Blakely|Jenibeth]] and [[Ollus Blakely]], whose parents, [[Terrin Blakely|Terrin]] and [[Alyst Blakely|Alyst]], had [[Suicide|killed themselves]] to prevent the Daleks from obtaining the information on the Cradle they possessed.

After learning more about the Cradle on the [[desert]] planet of [[Gethria]] and losing Jenibeth, the Doctor tried to spark a revolution on [[Sunlight 349]] to cause the collapse of the Dalek Foundation but he could not gather the necessary support. The Dalek Litigator arrived and subjected the Doctor to another public trial. Sabel and Ollus were taken away from the Doctor's care and he was exiled from the Sunlight Worlds. However he returned to Gethria 90 years in the future and encountered an elderly Jenibeth who had been transformed into a [[Dalek puppet]] after the Daleks took her prisoner as a child. The Dalek Time Controller arrived and forced the Doctor to activate the Cradle but Jenibeth's childlike mind allowed her to resist her conditioning and she fired on the Daleks, destroying numerous drones and forcing the Time Controller to retreat and the Doctor set the Cradle to self-destruct.

Before the Cradle exploded, it reverted the Sunlight Worlds to how Jenibeth remembered them as a child, as well as turning her and her siblings back into children and recreating their parents, although their memories were reverted too. The Daleks abandoned the plan. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[The Dalek Generation (novel)|The Dalek Generation]]'')

==== Fall of the Paradigm ====
{{Main|Reinvention of the Dalek Empire}}
Though the five initial members of the New Paradigm had been its ruling [[Dalek Council]], their many failures eventually caused their followers to revolt against them, reinstating the [[Parliament of the Daleks]] as the new ruling body of the Dalek Empire. Among the first acts of the newly instated [[Prime Minister of the Daleks]] was to turn the Paradigm's unique style of casing into a seldom seen "officer class" design and return the active infantry to those designs used in the Last Great Time War. Paradigm Daleks were subsequently reduced to a token presence in the Parliament, with the [[resurrected Dalek Empire]] ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}) largely being composed of bronze Daleks. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Asylum of the Daleks (TV story)}})

==== Forgetting the Doctor ====
The Daleks were notable customers of the information regarding [[the Doctor]] held by the [[Inforarium]]. When the Eleventh Doctor discovered the Daleks, as well as the [[Cyberman|Cybermen]] and [[Sontaran]]s, had been purchasing this information, he infiltrated the Inforarium and memory-proofed their database using methods he learned from [[Silent|the Silence]]. The information sold was thus instantly forgotten. ([[HOMEVID]]: {{cs|The Inforarium (home video)}})

When a [[human]] [[starliner]], the ''[[Alaska (spaceship)|Alaska]]'', crashlanded on the [[Dalek Asylum]] [[planet]], the security of the insane Daleks contained there was compromised. Fearing what would happen if these Daleks were to escape, the Prime Minister ordered the abduction of the Doctor, who he knew as the predator of the Daleks, so he could be sent to the Asylum and lower its impenetrable [[force field]] so the Daleks could destroy their deranged brethren, despite their wish to preserve them and their "beautiful" hatred. Understanding that the Doctor was best assisted by his [[companion]]s, his most recent ones, [[Amy Pond]] and [[Rory Williams]], were abducted as well.

Once the planet's defences were lowered by the human-turned-Dalek, [[Oswin Oswald]], the Parliament launched an attack to destroy the Asylum, but not before Oswin wiped out all memory of the Doctor in the minds of every Dalek. When the Doctor came back to their ship, he was bombarded with "[[the Question]]" ("Doctor Who?") by the entire Parliament. He left shortly after, but not before taunting the bewildered Daleks that they'd never stop asking. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Asylum of the Daleks (TV story)}})

==== Siege of Trenzalore ====
The Daleks—along with the [[Cyberman|Cybermen]], [[Sontaran]]s, [[Slitheen]], [[Terileptil]]s, [[Silurian]]s, [[Judoon]], [[Weeping Angel]]s and many other species—were driven to [[Trenzalore]] by a [[The Question|mysterious message]], a question asked by the [[Time Lord]]s through a [[Time Field|crack in the universe]] with the answer being [[the Doctor]]'s true name. If it was answered, the Time Lords would return and the waiting [[fleet]]s would fire on them, beginning another [[time war]]. The [[Papal Mainframe]] arrived at the planet first and set up a [[force field]] which locked all the other species out of the planet and the [[Siege of Trenzalore]] began.

While the other species attempted to sneak past the force field, the Daleks called for reinforcements, preparing for war. Eventually they attacked the mainframe, killing everyone before converting them into [[Dalek puppet]]s. Information regarding the Doctor was harvested from [[Tasha Lem]], resulting in the Daleks remembering who he was. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Time of the Doctor (TV story)}}) The remembrance of the Doctor drove the [[Prime Minister of the Daleks]] insane, resulting in it being declared unfit for leadership and being exterminated by the [[Supreme Dalek (Victory of the Daleks)|Supreme]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}) They also revived, tortured, and killed Tasha "several times" in an effort to learn how to break the force field. The Daleks then arranged for the Doctor to be lured into a trap, but Tasha managed to break free from her conditioning and destroyed the Daleks sent to kill the Doctor.

[[File:Daleks destroyed at Trenzalore.jpg|thumb|Two Dalek ground fighters are blown apart by the blast of the Doctor's regeneration. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Time of the Doctor (TV story)}})|alt=]]Despite the trap failing, the Daleks managed to breach the force field, and the Siege of Trenzalore grew into a war as the species orbiting the planet followed the Daleks through the force field. After much fighting, many of these species were killed or retreated. The Doctor and the Mainframe's [[Silent]] priests acted as the last line of defence against the Daleks but they too were overpowered and the Doctor, having used up all twelve of his [[regeneration]]s, grew too old to continue fighting.

With the resistance dealt with, the Daleks began looking for the Doctor in the town of [[Christmas (town)|Christmas]] with [[Dalek fighter pod]]s firing on the town and a huge [[Dalek flying saucer|flying saucer]] descending upon it. However, [[Clara Oswald]] pleaded to the Time Lords to grant the Doctor a new regeneration cycle, and the Doctor began regenerating into his [[Twelfth Doctor|twelfth incarnation]]. The energy released was enough to destroy some of the attacking Fighter Pods and the final burst destroyed the command saucer ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Time of the Doctor (TV story)}}) and the rest of the Dalek fleet. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (novelisation)}}) The shockwave blew apart the Daleks ground forces, ending the war. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Time of the Doctor (TV story)}})

==== Resistance from within ====
The Daleks engaged in a race against the Cybermen to obtain the [[Orb of Fates]], the key to a [[Time Lord]] warship and superweapon called the ''[[Starbane]]''. One Dalek managed to obtain one piece of the Orb and hid it inside its casing after it was taken prisoner by two Cybermen and interrogated as to the artefact's whereabouts. The Dalek sent a [[distress signal]] which was answered by the Twelfth Doctor who flattened the interrogating Cybermen with his TARDIS. The Dalek, whom the Doctor called "[[Lumpy]]", claimed its nature had been altered by the Cybermen during its imprisonment and it expressed a desire to see both the Daleks and the Cybermen thwarted in their attempts to gain control of the ''Starbane''.

[[File:Daleks at Starbane.jpg|thumb|The Daleks, including those with [[White Dalek|white]], [[Green Dalek|green]], and [[Red Dalek|red casings]], occupy the ''[[Starbane]].'' ([[GAME]]: {{cs|The Doctor and the Dalek (video game)}})|alt=]]
The Doctor and Lumpy teamed up in an unlikely alliance. They discovered the two remaining elements of the Orb of Fates on [[Telos]] and on [[Sontar]] respectively - with the Doctor repairing Lumpy partially. Upon piecing back together the Orb, the TARDIS was transported directly to the ''Starbane''. However, by that point it was already under the occupation of the Dalek forces. As Lumpy proceeded deeper into the Starbane, he and the other Daleks soon revealed that Lumpy had never been changed and that the Daleks had tricked the Doctor into literally giving them control of the Starbane. However, the Twelfth Doctor revealed that when he was repairing Lumpy he fitted in a device to control Lumpy's armour and managed to get Lumpy to the core while he piloted his TARDIS away - with the Daleks pursuing Lumpy unable to catch him. Forcing Lumpy to throw the orb into the core, the Starbane and the Dalek forces inside were destroyed - although Lumpy survived in a badly damaged state, screaming the Doctor's name as the Doctor bid farewell to his unlikely companion. ([[GAME]]: {{cs|The Doctor and the Dalek (video game)}})

=== Return to Skaro and beyond ===
[[File:Daleks (Series 9).jpg|thumb|A [[Bronze Dalek|bronze]] [[Dalek drone|drone]], [[Supreme Dalek (The Magician's Apprentice)|Supreme Dalek]], and [[Black Dalek (The Magician's Apprentice)|Black Dalek]] on a rebuilt [[Skaro]]. ([[TV]]: The Magician's Apprentice)|alt=|left]]
A number of Daleks joined Davros (who survived the [[Crucible]]'s destruction) on a rebuilt Skaro, ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Magician's Apprentice (TV story)}}) which they made the centre of their empire ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}}) and where Davros was dying of advanced age. The Daleks, due to Davros having no control over them, captured and appeared to exterminate {{Gomez}} and Clara after the two tried to escape imprisonment on Skaro. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Magician's Apprentice (TV story)}})

Later, the [[Twelfth Doctor]] stole Davros' chair and trundled into [[Dalek control]], brandishing a severed gunstick. The Daleks attempted to exterminate the Doctor but failed, as the force field on Davros' chair still held after its owner left. The Daleks and Davros were later given some of the Doctor's regeneration energy to be fashioned into Time Lord-Dalek hybrids, but were defeated when the [[Dalek City]] was destroyed by the decomposing Daleks in the sewers below the city, whom had also been healed by the regeneration energy and revolted against the Daleks. The City was all but reduced to rubble and in the midst of the chaos Missy tried to escape, but was cornered by a large group of Daleks. Then she informed her captors that she had "a very clever idea". Additionally, having seen that the Dalek casing could say the word "mercy", the Doctor travelled back to Davros' childhood to teach the boy about mercy, ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}}) but the Time War-era Time Lords, studying the past and future of the Daleks, considered this a failure. From what they saw, the Doctor's actions had no effect on the timeline, as they found no evidence the Daleks of their time zone understood mercy. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek Combat Training Manual (reference book)}})

Missy spent some time on Skaro, even writing a postcard to the Doctor with a picture of herself in front of the Dalek City, ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Postcards from the Universe (short story)|Postcards from the Universe]]'') before escaping from the Daleks. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Liar, the Glitch and the War Zone (short story)}}) Davros also survived the encounter, writing a study on the Daleks to be used in case he ever died. In the report, he wrote that he was still connected to the life force of his children but that he also had the regeneration energy ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Secrets of the Dalek Laboratory (feature)}}) stolen from the Doctor. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}}) Believing the regeneration energy presented great prospects for the future, he concluded his study by stating all non-Dalek life needed to be destroyed. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Secrets of the Dalek Laboratory (feature)}})

As recounted by Missy, the "word among the Daleks" was that the Doctor was retired and on [[Darillium]], ([[TV]]: {{cs|Extremis (TV story)}}) following the Twelfth Doctor indeed spending twenty-four years on Darillium living a quiet married life with [[River Song]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Husbands of River Song (TV story)}}) Nevertheless, he would find himself chased by a [[Black Dalek (A Hero like the Doctor)|Black Dalek]] at one point, yet he managed to trap it before he escaped. ([[WC]]: {{cs|A Hero like the Doctor (webcast)}}) During his travels with Bill Potts, the Twelfth Doctor also encountered a [[Dalek harvest ship]]. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Harvest of the Daleks (comic story)}}) The Doctor also had a VHS copy of the [[Daleks' master plan]] in his TARDIS and, when he saw [[Archibald Hamish Lethbridge-Stewart]] hold up the tape, speculated to himself that the Daleks wanted to get the documentation back. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (novelisation)}})

[[File:Rusty lights lit up TUaT.jpg|thumb|[[Rusty (Into the Dalek)|Rusty]] billions of years into his crusade against the rest of the Dalek race. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (TV story)}})|alt=]]
A short time after that, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (novelisation)}}) seeking to learn the truth about the [[Testimony Foundation]], the Twelfth Doctor travelled to [[Villengard]] to access the Dalek [[pathweb]] from [[Rusty (Into the Dalek)|Rusty]], the very Dalek he had turned against the rest of the species much earlier in his life. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (TV story)}}) Still fighting though his casing showed signs of age and dilapidation, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (novelisation)}}) Rusty had spent billions of years destroying the Daleks, eventually having set himself up in a tower on Villengard where he stood watch, blasting apart the casings of all the Daleks sent by the rest of the empire to kill him. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (TV story)}}) Able to fire out the many windows in what appeared to be a former throne room, Rusty was hooked into machines that, based on the Doctor's assumptions at least, were keeping the mutant live. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (novelisation)}})

Many of the Daleks Rusty blasted managed to survive the destruction of their casings, left to crawl around the ruins without their travel machines for as long as they could. When the Doctor arrived, he convinced Rusty to help him learn about Testimony, citing that helping him in any way would hurt the rest of the Daleks. Rusty provided the Doctor with the information he wanted before the Time Lord, who had been joined by his [[First Doctor|first incarnation]], a glass avatar of Bill Potts, and [[Captain]] [[Archibald Hamish Lethbridge-Stewart]], departed from Rusty's lair, having learned Testimony was not a nefarious organisation. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (TV story)}})

=== Enemies of the Thirteenth Doctor ===
Although the Twelfth Doctor had reminded her that the Daleks were the only constant throughout their lives as he regenerated into her, ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|The Many Lives of Doctor Who (comic story)}}) the Thirteenth Doctor implied she had thought herself free from the threat of the Daleks until she encountered the [[Reconnaissance Dalek]] from early Dalek history, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resolution (TV story)}})

At some point in or prior to [[2020]], the Daleks once more took control of Earth. [[Dalek (Incoming Transmission)|One]] took control of a [[bbcdoctorwho|social media account]] with [[million]]s of [[follower]]s, through which it declared the victory of the Daleks and ordered that it be celebrated as [[Dalek Day]]. However, the Doctor soon began to interfere with the transmission, and a few moments later, the Daleks left Earth, albeit vowing to come back by [[1 January]] [[2021]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Incoming Transmission (audio story)}})

[[File:Dalek Death Squad.jpg|thumb|The [[Death Squad Dalek|Death Squad]] that was lured to Earth by the [[Thirteenth Doctor]] to fight the [[Defence Drone|New Dalek Army]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revolution of the Daleks (TV story)}})|alt=|left]]
On that day, ([[WC]]: ''[[The Defence Drones (webcast)|The Defence Drones]]'') the Thirteenth Doctor summoned a [[Death Squad Dalek|Dalek Death Squad]] that was stationed in the [[Time Vortex]] to the Earth, forcing them into a confrontation with [[Defense drone|a force]] of impure Daleks, which had been created by a clone of the [[Reconnaissance Dalek]] she had previously fought, during their [[2021 Dalek revolution|invasion of England]]. After the defeat of the so-called New Dalek Army, the Death Squad's [[Dalek Death Squad spacecraft|flying saucer]] was destroyed by explosives planted by the Doctor's companions. The remaining units were lured into [[TARDIS 1 (The Timeless Children)|a spare TARDIS]] by the Doctor, who had programmed the TARDIS to fold in on itself and then dispose of itself in [[the Void]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revolution of the Daleks (TV story)}})

When [[King (The Death List)|a King]] wanted her dead, the Doctor ran across hills and hid behind a Dalek. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[The Death List (short story)|The Death List]]'')

=== Facing the Flux ===
During the [[Great Disruption]] caused by [[the Flux]] and the [[Ravager (The Halloween Apocalypse)|Ravagers]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|Once, Upon Time (TV story)}}) that made "time run wild", the Dalek Empire, like other hostile powers, tried to assert its power, exploiting the power vacuum and lack of opposition. The Daleks expanded their empire quickly, with their "borders" growing to encompass a sector—which [[Bel (Once, Upon Time)|Bel]] dubbed the "[[Dalek Sector]]" as she tried to escape it—of the galaxy, including conquering abandoned [[Lupar]]i space. In effect, powers like the Daleks, the [[Cybermen]], and the [[Sontaran Empire]] were acting as they always did, expanding and fighting for, as Bel put it, "the spoils" amid a universe–wide destruction. As such, she hoped that the three powers would destroy each other in the end.

After avoiding a Dalek patrol on a [[Dalek-invaded planet (Once, Upon Time)|forested world]], Bel managed to barely escape the sector while under fire from Daleks, later avoiding the expanding borders of the Dalek Empire once again after escaping a [[Cyberman-invaded planet (Once, Upon Time)|Cyberman-invaded planet]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Once, Upon Time (TV story)}}) As the Flux continued to rage, the Daleks knew the danger it posed to themselves, so they and the Cybermen agreed to meet the Sontarans to form an alliance. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Vanquishers (TV story)}}) The [[Dalek War Fleet]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|Eve of the Daleks (TV story)}}) was sent to the designated location in the year [[2021]], but the Sontarans had tricked their rivals and, once all Dalek and Cyber battalions had arrived, the Sontarans shielded behind a [[battalion wall]] of [[Lupari]] vessels intending to let the Flux ravage the [[Dalek flying saucer]]s and [[Cyber-ship]]s, only for the Sontarans themselves to be left outside of the shield due to the Doctor's meddling, leaving their craft to face the same fate as the Daleks and Cybermen. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Vanquishers (TV story)}})

[[File:Dalek Executioner 2.jpg|thumb|right|A [[Dalek Executioner]] in [[2021]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|Eve of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
The Daleks suffered mass causalities at the end of the Flux event through the destruction of their fleet, but, as written by [[Clara Oswald]], "a few" were able to survive to continue their empire. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[Whotopia: The Ultimate Guide to the Whoniverse (reference book)|Whotopia: The Ultimate Guide to the Whoniverse]]'') After realising her role in the destruction of the War Fleet and locating her TARDIS in [[ELF Storage]] on [[New Year's Eve]] in 2021, three [[Dalek Executioner|Executioner Daleks]] were dispatched to execute the Doctor by [[Dalek High Command]]. When they succeeded, the damaged TARDIS created a [[time loop]], which repeatedly resurrected her as the Daleks kept killing her. Eventually, she lured the Executioner Daleks to a pile of explosives she'd arranged to detonate, destroying them. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Eve of the Daleks (TV story)}})

=== Alliance with the Master and Cybermen ===
{{Main|The Master's Dalek Plan}}
The rage the Daleks felt towards the Doctor was used by {{Dhawan}} to convince them to ally with him and the [[Cyberman|Cybermen]]; inspired by [[Team TARDIS|the Doctor's "fam"]], he promised them that, together, they would finally be able to destroy the Doctor and conquer the Earth. Per what he dubbed "[[the Master's Dalek Plan]]", while the Master forced the Doctor to undergo a [[forced regeneration]] into himself and tarnished [[The Doctor (title)|their name]], the Earth would be left to the Daleks and Cybermen to become a production planet, but both sides displayed different understandings of the plan's end goal: the Cybermen under [[Ashad]] wanted to convert humanity into a new [[Cyber-Army]], while the Daleks wanted to wipe out the entire human population. To fulfil the plan, a force of [[Bronze Dalek]]s under a [[Dalek Commander (The Power of the Doctor)|Bronze Commander]] travelled to [[Bolivia]] in [[2022]] to force all of Earth's [[volcano]]s to erupt and wipe out humanity. The Daleks also became aware of how the Master had destroyed Gallifrey, as he was willing to admit as such in their presence during their plot.

[[File:Daleks capture Thirteenth Dr Who.jpg|thumb|left|Daleks capture the Thirteenth Doctor during [[The Master's Dalek Plan]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Power of the Doctor (TV story)}})]]
At the same time, the Daleks discovered a [[Dalek traitor|traitor in their ranks]]; a Dalek drone had come to the conclusion that its race had failed because, instead of keeping the [[Kaled]] race alive, the Daleks had become devoted to their own survival as the supposed supreme beings of the universe. To entrap the Doctor, the Daleks allowed the traitor to contact the Doctor's TARDIS and offer her a chance to destroy their entire race. Although overwhelmed by the reemergence of the [[CyberMaster]]s and the Master himself, the Doctor agreed to meet with the traitor upon learning the Daleks were preparing a new invasion of Earth. While meeting with the traitor, however, the Doctor and it were cornered by three Daleks, who exterminated the traitor and forced the Doctor to enter its casing before she could escape with its intel. The Daleks forced the casing to perform a [[spatial temporal shift]] and travel to [[St Petersburg]] in [[1916]], where several Daleks and CyberMasters watched as the Master carried out the forced regeneration with power supplied by a [[conversion planet]] he had the Cybermen create.

After waiting for him to return from destroying two planets and give the word, the Daleks in 1916 returned to the overall force in 2022 to carry out the eruption plot, unaware that their operation had been infiltrated by [[Ace]] and [[Graham O'Brien]]. After Ace and Graham destroyed a Dalek standing guard, they detonated the controls to the operation with [[Nitro-9]], leaving the volcano to erupt around the Daleks. When the Doctor, [[Retro-regeneration|restored to her true self]] by Yaz and [[Inston-Vee Vinder]], returned to 2022 to rescue Ace and Graham, the Daleks realised she had survived the Master's plan, but she managed to escape their pursuit. The Dalek force on Earth was destroyed by the volcano as they attempted to flee. The Doctor then used the conversion planet to stop the eruptions around the Earth, saving the planet from the Daleks' interference. She was, however, fatally injured by the Master in his final moments, leading to her regeneration into the [[Fourteenth Doctor]], ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Power of the Doctor (TV story)}}) whose first adventure resulted in him being embroiled in the [[Dalek Dome]]'s [[1966 Dalek invasion of Earth]] attraction. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Liberation of the Daleks (comic story)}})

After the Master's Dalek Plan, a [[Group (Wanted! Daleks)|group]] allied with [[UNIT]] ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Wanted! Cybermen (feature)}}) put out an arrest warrant on the Daleks under [[Article 412 of the Shadow Proclamation]]. The group listed the Daleks' "current status" as having endured multiple "extinction events" that "devastated" their fleet, but the group still warned the Daleks always survived such crises. As such, it asked anyone reading to be on high alert. That the group felt the need to put out an arrest warrant on the Daleks proved they were still alive. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Wanted! Daleks (feature)}})

=== Hypothesised final defeat ===
In the year [[200,100]], the Daleks were thought by humanity to have disappeared "thousands of years ago", as they had left to fight the [[Last Great Time War]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}}) The [[Final Dalek War]] was a hypothesised future war that was supposedly started by Skaro's penultimate destruction. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Infinity Doctors (novel)}}) According to one account, Skaro was destroyed via an implosion in the "unforeseeable future", by which time [[Zone X Dalek]]s existed. ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|The Test of Time (comic story)}}) Alternatively, [[Jack Harkness]] believed that, thanks to Davros's engineering, the Daleks would be able to survive until the [[End of the universe|end of time]] itself. ([[WC]]: {{cs|Monster File: Davros (webcast)}})

Some historians from the [[Post-Time War universe]] considered that the Daleks' final defeat could have been at the [[Siege of Trenzalore]]. However, the historians knew that the Daleks remained active on Skaro, hidden behind its invisibility barrier, and concluded that the species survived. However, they believed that anytime the Daleks took up arms against the universe, they would be defeated. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}) Indeed, while they believed that their [[The Matrix|Matrix]] extrapolations of their foes' future should be taken as theoretical, the Time Lords of the Last Great Time War stated that the Daleks would survive beyond the Siege of Trenzalore, dating [[Hybrid Incident|the Twelfth Doctor's visit to Skaro]] occurring some time after it. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek Combat Training Manual (reference book)}})

The Daleks were all wiped out by the God of Death [[Sutekh]], when they, like the rest of the universe, fell victim to his plot to create a [[Susan Triad|woman]] wherever the Doctor's TARDIS landed, who would spread the [[Sutekh's Dust of Death|Dust of Death]]. This was notably observed by [[Fifteenth Doctor|The Doctor]] and much to the astonishment of [[Melanie Bush]]. However, they were all restored once the Doctor defeated Sutekh. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Empire of Death (TV story)}})

=== Undated events ===
==== War with the Galactic Resistance ====
{{Main|Dalek invasion of the galaxy}}
[[File:DalekParadigmITD.jpg|thumb|right|The Daleks during their war against the [[Combined Galactic Resistance]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Into the Dalek (TV story)}})]]
At some point in their history, the Daleks waged a war against the [[Combined Galactic Resistance]]. Though a Dalek unit, named [[Rusty (Into the Dalek)|Rusty]] by the [[Twelfth Doctor]], possessed access to data from events that succeeded the [[Last Great Time War]], ([[TV]]: {{cs|Into the Dalek (TV story)}}) with even the [[Time Lord]]s believing the unit to have come from a time after the [[Siege of Trenzalore]], ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek Combat Training Manual (reference book)}}) several accounts placed the Dalek as operating during the reign of the [[Dalek Empire]], either during the [[Dalek Wars]] or the [[Great War (The Evil of the Daleks)|Great War]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}, {{cs|The Secret Lives of Monsters (short story)}}, {{cs|The Whoniverse (novel)}}) During the conflict against the resistance, the Daleks gained a major presence in the [[Ryzak solar system]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Secret Lives of Monsters (short story)}})

After the [[Twelfth Doctor]] rescued [[Journey Blue]], the Resistance asked him to help fix Rusty as he had been turned [[good]]. The Doctor, Clara Oswald, Journey and two soldiers travelled into Rusty and located a crack in his power source that was spewing radiation and killing him, losing one soldier along the way. The Doctor repaired the crack with [[the Doctor's sonic screwdriver|his sonic screwdriver]], but the radiation had been causing the Dalek's change and it turned evil again, breaking free of its restraints and calling in more Daleks to destroy the ''[[Aristotle (spaceship)|Aristotle]]''. At the insistence of Clara, the Doctor, Clara, Journey and the remaining soldier attempted to turn Rusty good again by reactivating his suppressed memories, particularly that of a star being born which would open him to the Doctor's influence. Clara succeeded in reactivating the memories, opening Rusty's mind and the Doctor [[telepathy|telepathically]] linked with him to get him to see the good in the universe through the Doctor. However, the "beauty" that Rusty saw was the destruction of the Daleks by the Doctor in the past and realising they were [[evil]], Rusty turned on the Daleks who were attacking the human resistance fighters and slaughtered them.

After Rusty's victory, and after telling the Doctor that he wasn't a good Dalek but the Doctor was, Rusty ordered the [[Dalek ship (Into the Dalek)|Dalek flying saucer]] that was docked with the ''Aristotle'' to retreat, claiming that the humans had activated the ship's self-destruct then left with them to continue his war against his own kind. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Into the Dalek (TV story)}}) According to the research of human historians, Rusty managed to destroy his saucer but was left adrift in space. Upon being recovered, Rusty was brought before the ruling [[Dalek Council]] who called off their invasion out of fear that Rusty's hatred could spread to other units. Finding his hatred too beautiful to destroy however, the Council exiled Rusty to the [[Dalek Asylum]] for his deviance, ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}}) though he managed to escape the planet before its destruction, continuing his crusade against his own kind over billions of years. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (TV story)}}, [[PROSE]]: {{cs|Twice Upon a Time (novelisation)}})

A [[bronze Dalek]] arrived in the [[River Thames]] on [[19 August]] [[2020]] through the [[Time Fracture]]. The Dalek was quickly intercepted by military personnel before it could harm civilians. ([[WC]]: ''[[14683 UNIT Field Log (webcast)|14683 UNIT Field Log]]'')

[[Bel (Once, Upon Time)|Bel]] and [[Inston-Vee Vinder]] had experience fighting the Daleks before [[the Flux]] event. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Once, Upon Time (TV story)}})

At some point in their history, the Daleks nearly succeeded in conquering Earth, as [[the Doctor]] was distracted by reading ''[[Diary of a Wimpy Kid]]''. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Nightmare Realm (audio story)|The Nightmare Realm]]'')

=== Alternate timelines ===
In an [[alternate timeline (The Ripple Effect)|alternate timeline]] created when the [[Seventh Doctor]]'s [[The Doctor's TARDIS|TARDIS]] got trapped in the [[Temporal Plexus]], the Daleks were peace-loving academics, with [[Skaro]] being the universal centre of [[civilisation]], [[philosophy]], [[democracy]] and [[art]]. The [[Time Lord]]s of this timeline were on good terms with these Daleks. Ultimately the Seventh Doctor erased this timeline from [[existence]] when it began to threaten the stability of the original timeline. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[The Ripple Effect (short story)|The Ripple Effect]]'')

In an [[Alternate timeline (Time & Time Again)|alternate timeline]] created by the [[Black Guardian]], in which the [[First Doctor]] never left [[Gallifrey]] and instead became [[President of the High Council|Lord President]], the Daleks had amassed an enormous empire that even the Time Lords feared. The [[Imperial Dalek]]s were among the twelve species that invaded [[Earth]] at the same time. This timeline was erased when the Seventh Doctor acquired the [[Key to Time]], on the instructions of the [[White Guardian]]. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[Time & Time Again (comic story)|Time & Time Again]]'')

In one timeline in which the First Doctor's TARDIS never landed on [[Kembel]], the Daleks successfully developed the [[Time Destructor]] and embarked on an uncontested campaign of conquest through [[space]]. After reaching the [[Third Galaxy]], they [[Annihilation|annihilated]] the planet [[Baralda]] intent on forcing the swift [[surrender]] of neighbouring [[Urbinia]] for use of its [[population]] as [[slave]] labour. The [[Harvesting of Urbinia|ensuing crisis]] pitched the Daleks against the [[multi-Doctor Event|First and Second Doctors]], and in the absence of a meaningful surrender, the [[Black Dalek Leader|Dalek Supreme]] opted to destroy the planet. However, the [[Second Doctor]] averted the timeline by preventing the [[Temporal collision|initial collision]] which had sent the First Doctor to Urbinia instead of Kembel. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Daughter of the Gods (audio story)|Daughter of the Gods]]'')

[[File:Dalek (The Master's Dalek Plan).jpg|left|thumb|The [[aborted timeline]] [[Dalek (The Master's Dalek Plan)|Daleks]] created by {{Jacobi}} after he [[Murder|killed]] a young [[Davros]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Master's Dalek Plan (audio story)}})]]
In an [[aborted timeline]], {{Jacobi}} used the [[Anti-Genesis code]]s to travel from the [[Last Great Time War]] to Skaro during the [[Thousand Year War]], where he killed [[Davros]] ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[From the Flames (audio story)|From the Flames]]'') and infiltrated the [[Kaled]] [[Scientific Elite]] to create his own race of [[Dalek (The Master's Dalek Plan)|Daleks]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Master's Dalek Plan (audio story)}}, ''[[Shockwave (TWM audio story)|Shockwave]]'') In this timeline, the Daleks successfully conquered the universe, but gradually developed a resentment of their creator, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|He Who Wins (audio story)}}) as the Daleks had with Davros in the original timeline. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}} et al.) Ultimately, these Daleks were erased from existence in a combined effort from the Master's future self, a [[Unbound Master|parallel universe Master]], and the [[Dalek Time Strategist (The Shadow Vortex)|Dalek Time Strategist]], as the Master's rewriting of the Daleks' [[history]] threatened to erase all of creation. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|He Who Wins (audio story)}})

In [[Alternate timeline (The Death of Captain Jack)|an alternate timeline]] where [[John Hart (Kiss Kiss, Bang Bang)|John Hart]] was the [[King of England]], Hart had [[Torchwood One]] open the [[Void Ship]]. Thus, the Daleks destroyed Torchwood One and the majority of the [[home counties]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[The Death of Captain Jack (audio story)|The Death of Captain Jack]]'')

In an [[Cyber-President's timeline|alternate timeline]] where [[Rassilon]] and the [[Cyberiad]] allied to conquer all of [[time]] and [[space]], the Cybermen conquered Skaro and erased the Daleks from history. The Daleks were restored when the [[Twelfth Doctor]] and Rassilon used the [[Eye of Harmony]] on Gallifrey to restore the original timeline. ([[COMIC]]: ''[[Prologue: The Fifth Doctor (comic story)|Prologue: The Fifth Doctor]]'', ''[[Supremacy of the Cybermen (comic story)|Supremacy of the Cybermen]]'')

In a number of timelines scavenged by [[Sibling Same]] and [[Different (Canaries)|Sibling Different]] to create the [[Paradox TARDIS]], the Daleks fused with the [[Bad Wolf (entity)|Bad Wolf entity]], causing metal copies of [[Rose Tyler]] to populate all of time and space. In addition, some of the components of [[the Doctor's TARDIS]] that the duo stole from the timelines they explored were scarred with energy fire from Daleks. ([[PROSE]]: ''[[The Paradox Moon (short story)|The Paradox Moon]]'')

In an aborted timeline, [[Unbound Master|the Master of a parallel universe]] attempted to use the Daleks of [[N-Space]] to destroy the [[entropy wave]], a representation of [[the Master]] of N-Space's final [[incarnation]], but the Daleks failed and were completely destroyed. This timeline was eventually erased after the entropy wave consumed several of the N-Space Master's incarnations, including {{Gomez}}, thereby creating a [[Temporal paradox|paradox]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Masterful (audio story)|Masterful]]'')

=== Alternate universes ===
In a [[parallel universe]] created by the [[Quantum Archangel]], the Daleks were [[the Enemy]] in the [[War in Heaven]]. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Quantum Archangel (novel)}})

The [[Dalek Emperor (The Genocide Machine)|Dalek Emperor]] once summoned [[Dalek (Project Infinity)|Daleks]] from a [[The Mentor's universe|parallel universe]] for assistance in conquering [[Mutter's Spiral]]. These Daleks, however, were appalled by the actions of their counterparts, who they termed "Enemy Daleks" as they sided with the remnants of the [[Earth Alliance]] against the [[Dalek Empire]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Project Infinity (audio story)}}, ''[[Dalek Empire II: Dalek War]]'')

The [[Thalek (Auld Mortality)|Thaleks]] existed in the universe of [[The Doctor (Auld Mortality)|another Doctor]]. ([[AUDIO]]: ''[[Auld Mortality (audio story)|Auld Mortality]]'', [[PROSE]]: ''[[The Innocents (short story)|The Innocents]]'')

[[File:Dalek (Masters of War).jpeg|thumb|The [[Dalek (Unbound Universe)|Daleks]] from the [[Unbound Universe]], whose species' creation was influenced by the [[Quatch]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Masters of War (audio story)}})|alt=]]
In the [[Unbound Universe]], the [[Dalek (Unbound Universe)|Daleks]] split into two factions after the disappearance of their creator, [[Davros (Unbound Universe|Davros]]. One Dalek faction remained loyal to Davros and left [[Skaro (Unbound Universe)|Skaro]] to search for him, and the other went renegade and began an interstellar empire, encountering [[Unbound Doctor|the Doctor]] on several occasions and attacking Earth in 1972. The loyalists eventually returned to Skaro to protect the Thals from the [[Quatch]], the species responsible for the devastation of Skaro. The Doctor and [[Alistair Gordon Lethbridge-Stewart (Unbound Universe)|Alistair Lethbridge-Stewart]] arrived and, after discovering the true purpose of the Daleks' return home, helped the Thals and Daleks defend against the Quatch. The Doctor discovered Davros was working with the Quatch and persuaded him to turn on them by revealing their role in Skaro's devastation. After the Quatch's defeat, the Daleks and Thals decided to live in peace together on Skaro, with Alistair staying to assist. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Masters of War (audio story)}})
